Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 20, verse 1–8 (part 1 of 2):

Tafsir of Surat Ta-Ha

It is Meccan.

The Imam of the Imams Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Khuzayma related in his book "al-Tawhid," from Ziyad ibn Ayyub, from Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir al-Hizami, who said: Ibrahim ibn Muhajir ibn Mismar narrated to us, from Umar ibn Hafs ibn Dhakwan, from the mawla of al-Hurqa (meaning Abd al-Rahman ibn Yaqub), from Abu Hurayra, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah recited Ta-Ha and Ya-Sin one thousand years before He created Adam. When the angels heard it, they said: 'Blessed is the community upon which this will be sent down, blessed are the bodies that will carry this, and blessed are the tongues that will speak this.'" [The Tawhid (p. 109). It was also related by Ibn Abi Asim in al-Sunna (no. 607) and al-Lalaka'i in Sharh Usul I'tiqad Ahl al-Sunna (no. 368), through Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir with the same chain. Ibn Hibban said: "This is a fabricated text (matn mawdu')." Ibn Adi said: "I did not find for Ibrahim (i.e., Ibn Muhajir) a narration more objectionable than this, since no one other than him narrates it."]

This is a gharib (strange) hadith, and it contains nakara (objectionable content), and Ibrahim ibn Muhajir and his shaykh have been criticized.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

* *

The discussion of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'a) has already been covered at the beginning of Surat al-Baqara, sufficiently so that it need not be repeated.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Shanba al-Wasiti narrated to us, Abu Ahmad (i.e., al-Zubayri) narrated to us, Israil informed us, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, who said: "Ta-Ha" means "O man." This is also related from Mujahid, Ikrima, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Ata', Muhammad ibn Ka'b, Abu Malik, Atiyya al-Awfi, al-Hasan, Qatada, al-Dahhak, al-Suddi, and Ibn Abza, that they said: "Ta-Ha" means "O man."

In another narration from Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and al-Thawri, it is a word in Nabataean meaning "O man." Abu Salih said it is arabized (mu'arraba).

Qadi Iyad, in his book "al-Shifa," cited through the chain of Abd ibn Humayd in his Tafsir: Hashim ibn [al-Qasim] narrated to us, from Ibn Ja'far, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, who said: When the Prophet ﷺ prayed, he would stand on one foot and raise the other. So Allah the Exalted revealed "Ta-Ha," meaning: "Step on the earth, O Muhammad." "We did not send down the Qur'an upon you to make you wretched." Then he said: There is no concealment of the honour and the excellent treatment contained in this.

* *

As for His saying "We did not send down the Qur'an upon you to make you wretched": Juwaybir related from al-Dahhak: When Allah sent down the Qur'an upon His Messenger, he and his companions stood in prayer with it, and the polytheists of Quraysh said: "This Qur'an was only sent down upon Muhammad to make him wretched!" So Allah the Exalted revealed: "Ta-Ha. We did not send down the Qur'an upon you to make you wretched, but as a reminder for one who fears."

The matter is not as the falsifiers claim. Rather, whoever Allah grants knowledge has been granted much good, as is established in the two Sahihs from Mu'awiya, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whomever Allah intends good for, He grants him understanding of the religion." [Sahih al-Bukhari (no. 71) and Sahih Muslim (no. 1037).]

How excellent is the hadith that the Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani related on this subject, where he said:

Ahmad ibn Zuhayr narrated to us, al-Ala' ibn Salim narrated to us, Ibrahim al-Talaqani narrated to us, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Simak ibn Harb, from Tha'laba ibn al-Hakam, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah the Exalted says to the scholars on the Day of Resurrection, when He sits upon His Throne to judge His servants: 'I have not placed My knowledge and My wisdom in you except that I intend to forgive you for what was from you, and I do not mind.'" [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (2/84). al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/126): "its narrators are trustworthy."]

Its isnad is good. This Tha'laba ibn al-Hakam [who is al-Laythi] was mentioned by Abu Umar in his al-Istiab, who said: He settled in Basra, then moved to Kufa, and Simak ibn Harb narrated from him.

Mujahid said regarding His saying "We did not send down the Qur'an upon you to make you wretched": it is like His saying "So recite what is easy of it" [al-Muzzammil: 20]; and they used to tie ropes to their chests during prayer.

Qatada said: "We did not send down the Qur'an upon you to make you wretched." No, by Allah, He did not make it a wretchedness, but He made it a mercy, a light, and a guide to Paradise.

"But as a reminder for one who fears": Allah sent down His Book and sent His Messengers as a mercy with which He showed compassion to the servants, so that the one who remembers may remember, and a man may benefit from what he hears of the Book of Allah, which is a reminder in which Allah has revealed its lawful and its unlawful.

* *

As for His saying: "A revelation from He who created the earth and the high heavens": that is, this Qur'an that has come to you, O Muhammad, is a revelation from your Lord, the Lord and Sovereign of all things, the One Capable of what He wills, who created the earth with its lowness and density, and created the high heavens in their height and subtlety. There has come in a hadith, which al-Tirmidhi and others declared sound, that the thickness of each heaven is a five hundred years' journey, and the distance between it and the one next to it is a five hundred years' journey. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi (no. 3298), from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said: "This is a gharib hadith from this route."]

Ibn Abi Hatim has cited here the hadith of the awʻal (mountain goats) through the narration of al-Abbas, the uncle of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, may Allah be pleased with him. [The hadith of the awʻal will come in full at the commentary on verse 7 of Surat Ghafir.]

* *

As for His saying "The Most Merciful sat firmly upon the Throne": the discussion of this has already been covered in Surat al-A'raf, sufficiently so that it need not be repeated. The safest path regarding it is the way of the Salaf: letting pass what has come concerning it in the Book and the Sunna without asking how (takyif), without distortion (tahrif), without likening (tashbih), without denial (ta'til), and without modelling (tamthil).

* *

As for His saying: "To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is beneath the soil": that is, all of it is His possession, in His grasp, under His disposal, His will, His determination, and His judgment. He is the Creator of that, its Owner, and its God; there is no god besides Him, and no lord other than Him.

* *

As for His saying "whatever is beneath the soil": Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: that is, what is beneath the seventh earth.

Al-Awza'i said: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir told him that Ka'b was asked, and it was said to him: "What is beneath this earth?" He said: "Water." It was said: "And what is beneath the water?" He said: "Earth." It was said: "And what is beneath the earth?" He said: "Water." It was said: "And what is beneath the water?" He said: "Earth." It was said: "And what is beneath the earth?" He said: "Water." It was said: "And what is beneath the water?" He said: "Earth." It was said: "And what is beneath the earth?" He said: "A rock." It was said: "And what is beneath the rock?" He said: "An angel." It was said: "And what is beneath the angel?" He said: "A fish whose two ends are suspended from the Throne." It was said: "And what is beneath the fish?" He said: "Air and darkness," and knowledge ended there.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Ubayd Allah, the nephew of Ibn Wahb, narrated to us; my uncle narrated to us; Abd Allah ibn Ayyash narrated to us; Abd Allah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Darraj, from Isa ibn Hilal al-Sadafi, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The earths, between each earth and the one next to it, are a five hundred years' journey, and the uppermost of them rests on the back of a fish whose two ends have met in the sky, and the fish is upon a rock, and the rock is in the hand of an angel, and the second is the prison of the wind, and the third contains the stones of Hell, and the fourth contains the sulphur of Hell, and the fifth contains the serpents of Hell, and the sixth contains the scorpions of Hell, and the seventh contains Saqar, and in it is Iblis, shackled with iron, one hand before him and one hand behind him; when Allah wills to release him for what He wills, He releases him." [Ibn Mandah related it in Kitab al-Tawhid (no. 63) through Harmala ibn Yahya from Abd Allah ibn Wahb, similarly. al-Hakim related it in al-Mustadrak (4/594) through Bahr ibn Nasr from Abd Allah ibn Wahb, from Abd Allah ibn Ayyash, from Abd Allah ibn Sulayman, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Isa ibn Hilal, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, with the like, but he added Abu al-Haytham to the isnad. He said: "Sahih but they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi criticized him. I say: rather, it is munkar; in it is Abd Allah ibn Ayyash, whom Abu Dawud declared weak, while in Muslim he is trustworthy, and Darraj is one who narrates many objectionable reports.]

This is a very gharib hadith, and its attribution to the Prophet is questionable.

Abu Ya'la al-Hafiz said in his Musnad: Abu Musa al-Harawi narrated to us, from al-Abbas ibn al-Fadl [who said]: I said: Ibn al-Fadl al-Ansari? He said: Yes, [from al-Qasim] ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the expedition of Tabuk, and we were returning in intense heat, scattered in ones and twos, dispersed. I was at the front of the army when a man confronted us, greeted, and then said: "Which of you is Muhammad?" My companions passed on and I stood with him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in the middle of the army on a red camel, with his garment covering his head against the sun. I said: "O questioner, this is the Messenger of Allah; he has come to you." He said: "Which of them is he?" I said: "The owner of the red young camel." So he approached him, took hold of the reins of his mount, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ halted. He said: "Are you Muhammad?" He said: "Yes." He said: "I want to ask you about matters which none of the people of the earth know except one or two men." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Ask whatever you wish." He said: "O Muhammad, does the Prophet sleep?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "His eyes sleep, but his heart does not sleep." He said: "You have spoken truly." Then he said: "O Muhammad, from where does a child resemble its father and its mother?" He said: "The man's water is white and thick, and the woman's water is yellow and thin; whichever of the two waters overcomes the other, the child takes after it." He said: "You have spoken truly." He said: "What belongs to the man from the child, and what belongs to the woman from it?" He said: "For the man: the bones, the sinews and the nerves; for the woman: the flesh, the blood, the hair [and the liver]." He said: "You have spoken truly." Then he said: "O Muhammad, what is beneath this, meaning the earth?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A creation." He said: "And what is beneath them?" He said: "Earth." He said: "And what is beneath the earth?" He said: "Water." He said: "And what is beneath the water?" He said: "Darkness." He said: "And what is beneath the darkness?" He said: "Air." He said: "And what is beneath the air?" He said: "The moist earth (al-thara)." He said: "And what is beneath the moist earth?" Then the eyes of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ overflowed with weeping, and he said: "The knowledge of created beings ends at the knowledge of the Creator. O questioner, the one asked about it is no more knowing than the questioner." He said: "You have spoken truly; I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O people, do you know who this is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "This is Jibril, peace be upon him." [Ibn Mardawayh related it in his Tafsir as in al-Durr al-Manthur (5/552), from the hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him.]

This is a very gharib hadith, with a strange context. Al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman is alone in narrating it. Yahya ibn Ma'in said of him: "He is worth nothing." Abu Hatim al-Razi declared him weak, and Ibn Adi said: "He is not known."

I say: he has confused this hadith, something has entered into something else, and a hadith has entered into a hadith. It is possible that he did this deliberately, or that it was inserted into him; Allah knows best.

* *

Ibn Kathir's commentary on the verse ﴿And if you speak aloud, indeed He knows the secret and that which is more hidden.﴾

Meaning: He sent down this Qur'an, the One who created the earth and the lofty heavens, ﴿the One who knows the secret and that which is more hidden﴾, as Allah says: ﴿Say, "It was sent down by He who knows the secret [and utterance] within the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful."﴾ [Al-Furqan: 6].

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿He knows the secret and that which is more hidden﴾: "The secret is what the son of Adam conceals within himself, and 'that which is more hidden' is what is hidden from the son of Adam, of what he will do before he knows it. Allah knows all of that. His knowledge of what has passed and what remains is one knowledge, and all of creation is in that respect before Him like a single soul, as He says: ﴿Your creation and your resurrection are not but as [that of] a single soul﴾ [Luqman: 28]."

Ad-Dahhak said regarding it: "The secret is what you speak of within yourself, and 'that which is more hidden' is what you have not yet spoken of within yourself."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "You know what you conceal today, but you do not know what you will conceal tomorrow. Allah knows what you conceal today and what you will conceal tomorrow."

Mujahid said: "'That which is more hidden' means the whispering (al-waswasah)."

He also said, together with Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "'That which is more hidden' means what he will do of what he has not yet spoken of within himself."

* *

His saying ﴿Allah — there is no deity except Him. To Him belong the Most Beautiful Names﴾ [meaning: the One who sent down the Qur'an to you is Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Possessor of the Most Beautiful Names (al-Asma' al-Husna) and the Lofty Attributes].

The hadiths concerning the Most Beautiful Names have already been explained at the end of Surah "Al-A'raf", and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

Mujahid said regarding His saying "We did not send down the Qur'an upon you to make you wretched": it is like His saying "So recite what is easy of it" [al-Muzzammil: 20]; and they used to tie ropes to their chests during prayer.

Qatada said: "We did not send down the Qur'an upon you to make you wretched." No, by Allah, He did not make it a wretchedness, but He made it a mercy, a light, and a guide to Paradise.

"But as a reminder for one who fears": Allah sent down His Book and sent His Messengers as a mercy with which He showed compassion to the servants, so that the one who remembers may remember, and a man may benefit from what he hears of the Book of Allah, which is a reminder in which Allah has revealed its lawful and its unlawful.

* *

As for His saying: "A revelation from He who created the earth and the high heavens": that is, this Qur'an that has come to you, O Muhammad, is a revelation from your Lord, the Lord and Sovereign of all things, the One Capable of what He wills, who created the earth with its lowness and density, and created the high heavens in their height and subtlety. There has come in a hadith, which al-Tirmidhi and others declared sound, that the thickness of each heaven is a five hundred years' journey, and the distance between it and the one next to it is a five hundred years' journey. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi (no. 3298), from the hadith of Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, and he said: "This is a gharib hadith from this route."]

Ibn Abi Hatim has cited here the hadith of the awʻal (mountain goats) through the narration of al-Abbas, the uncle of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, may Allah be pleased with him. [The hadith of the awʻal will come in full at the commentary on verse 7 of Surat Ghafir.]

* *

As for His saying "The Most Merciful sat firmly upon the Throne": the discussion of this has already been covered in Surat al-A'raf, sufficiently so that it need not be repeated. The safest path regarding it is the way of the Salaf: letting pass what has come concerning it in the Book and the Sunna without asking how (takyif), without distortion (tahrif), without likening (tashbih), without denial (ta'til), and without modelling (tamthil).

* *

As for His saying: "To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth and whatever is between them and whatever is beneath the soil": that is, all of it is His possession, in His grasp, under His disposal, His will, His determination, and His judgment. He is the Creator of that, its Owner, and its God; there is no god besides Him, and no lord other than Him.

* *

As for His saying "whatever is beneath the soil": Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: that is, what is beneath the seventh earth.

Al-Awza'i said: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir told him that Ka'b was asked, and it was said to him: "What is beneath this earth?" He said: "Water." It was said: "And what is beneath the water?" He said: "Earth." It was said: "And what is beneath the earth?" He said: "Water." It was said: "And what is beneath the water?" He said: "Earth." It was said: "And what is beneath the earth?" He said: "Water." It was said: "And what is beneath the water?" He said: "Earth." It was said: "And what is beneath the earth?" He said: "A rock." It was said: "And what is beneath the rock?" He said: "An angel." It was said: "And what is beneath the angel?" He said: "A fish whose two ends are suspended from the Throne." It was said: "And what is beneath the fish?" He said: "Air and darkness," and knowledge ended there.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Ubayd Allah, the nephew of Ibn Wahb, narrated to us; my uncle narrated to us; Abd Allah ibn Ayyash narrated to us; Abd Allah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Darraj, from Isa ibn Hilal al-Sadafi, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The earths, between each earth and the one next to it, are a five hundred years' journey, and the uppermost of them rests on the back of a fish whose two ends have met in the sky, and the fish is upon a rock, and the rock is in the hand of an angel, and the second is the prison of the wind, and the third contains the stones of Hell, and the fourth contains the sulphur of Hell, and the fifth contains the serpents of Hell, and the sixth contains the scorpions of Hell, and the seventh contains Saqar, and in it is Iblis, shackled with iron, one hand before him and one hand behind him; when Allah wills to release him for what He wills, He releases him." [Ibn Mandah related it in Kitab al-Tawhid (no. 63) through Harmala ibn Yahya from Abd Allah ibn Wahb, similarly. al-Hakim related it in al-Mustadrak (4/594) through Bahr ibn Nasr from Abd Allah ibn Wahb, from Abd Allah ibn Ayyash, from Abd Allah ibn Sulayman, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Isa ibn Hilal, from Abd Allah ibn Amr, with the like, but he added Abu al-Haytham to the isnad. He said: "Sahih but they did not record it," and al-Dhahabi criticized him. I say: rather, it is munkar; in it is Abd Allah ibn Ayyash, whom Abu Dawud declared weak, while in Muslim he is trustworthy, and Darraj is one who narrates many objectionable reports.]

This is a very gharib hadith, and its attribution to the Prophet is questionable.

Abu Ya'la al-Hafiz said in his Musnad: Abu Musa al-Harawi narrated to us, from al-Abbas ibn al-Fadl [who said]: I said: Ibn al-Fadl al-Ansari? He said: Yes, [from al-Qasim] ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, who said: I was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the expedition of Tabuk, and we were returning in intense heat, scattered in ones and twos, dispersed. I was at the front of the army when a man confronted us, greeted, and then said: "Which of you is Muhammad?" My companions passed on and I stood with him. Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came in the middle of the army on a red camel, with his garment covering his head against the sun. I said: "O questioner, this is the Messenger of Allah; he has come to you." He said: "Which of them is he?" I said: "The owner of the red young camel." So he approached him, took hold of the reins of his mount, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ halted. He said: "Are you Muhammad?" He said: "Yes." He said: "I want to ask you about matters which none of the people of the earth know except one or two men." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Ask whatever you wish." He said: "O Muhammad, does the Prophet sleep?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "His eyes sleep, but his heart does not sleep." He said: "You have spoken truly." Then he said: "O Muhammad, from where does a child resemble its father and its mother?" He said: "The man's water is white and thick, and the woman's water is yellow and thin; whichever of the two waters overcomes the other, the child takes after it." He said: "You have spoken truly." He said: "What belongs to the man from the child, and what belongs to the woman from it?" He said: "For the man: the bones, the sinews and the nerves; for the woman: the flesh, the blood, the hair [and the liver]." He said: "You have spoken truly." Then he said: "O Muhammad, what is beneath this, meaning the earth?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A creation." He said: "And what is beneath them?" He said: "Earth." He said: "And what is beneath the earth?" He said: "Water." He said: "And what is beneath the water?" He said: "Darkness." He said: "And what is beneath the darkness?" He said: "Air." He said: "And what is beneath the air?" He said: "The moist earth (al-thara)." He said: "And what is beneath the moist earth?" Then the eyes of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ overflowed with weeping, and he said: "The knowledge of created beings ends at the knowledge of the Creator. O questioner, the one asked about it is no more knowing than the questioner." He said: "You have spoken truly; I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "O people, do you know who this is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "This is Jibril, peace be upon him." [Ibn Mardawayh related it in his Tafsir as in al-Durr al-Manthur (5/552), from the hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him.]

This is a very gharib hadith, with a strange context. Al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman is alone in narrating it. Yahya ibn Ma'in said of him: "He is worth nothing." Abu Hatim al-Razi declared him weak, and Ibn Adi said: "He is not known."

I say: he has confused this hadith, something has entered into something else, and a hadith has entered into a hadith. It is possible that he did this deliberately, or that it was inserted into him; Allah knows best.

* *

Ibn Kathir's commentary on the verse ﴿And if you speak aloud, indeed He knows the secret and that which is more hidden.﴾

Meaning: He sent down this Qur'an, the One who created the earth and the lofty heavens, ﴿the One who knows the secret and that which is more hidden﴾, as Allah says: ﴿Say, "It was sent down by He who knows the secret [and utterance] within the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is ever Forgiving and Merciful."﴾ [Al-Furqan: 6].

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿He knows the secret and that which is more hidden﴾: "The secret is what the son of Adam conceals within himself, and 'that which is more hidden' is what is hidden from the son of Adam, of what he will do before he knows it. Allah knows all of that. His knowledge of what has passed and what remains is one knowledge, and all of creation is in that respect before Him like a single soul, as He says: ﴿Your creation and your resurrection are not but as [that of] a single soul﴾ [Luqman: 28]."

Ad-Dahhak said regarding it: "The secret is what you speak of within yourself, and 'that which is more hidden' is what you have not yet spoken of within yourself."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "You know what you conceal today, but you do not know what you will conceal tomorrow. Allah knows what you conceal today and what you will conceal tomorrow."

Mujahid said: "'That which is more hidden' means the whispering (al-waswasah)."

He also said, together with Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "'That which is more hidden' means what he will do of what he has not yet spoken of within himself."

* *

His saying ﴿Allah — there is no deity except Him. To Him belong the Most Beautiful Names﴾ [meaning: the One who sent down the Qur'an to you is Allah, there is no deity except Him, the Possessor of the Most Beautiful Names (al-Asma' al-Husna) and the Lofty Attributes].

The hadiths concerning the Most Beautiful Names have already been explained at the end of Surah "Al-A'raf", and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

From this point onward, may He be blessed and exalted, He began to mention the story of Musa [upon him peace] [[Addition from MS F.]]: how the revelation came to him and how He spoke to him. This was after Musa had completed the term that was between him and his father-in-law in tending the sheep, and he set out with his family. It was said that he was heading for the land of Egypt, after his absence from it had lasted more than ten years, and his wife was with him. He lost his way. It was a wintry night. He halted at a place between ravines and mountains, in cold and winter, with clouds, darkness and fog. He began to strike a flint he had with him [[In MS F: "to him"]] in order to kindle a fire, as was his habit, but it produced no spark and nothing came out of it. While he was in this state, he perceived a fire from the side of the Tur, that is, a fire appeared to him from the side of the mountain there, on his right. So he said to his family, giving them good news: ﴿Indeed, I have perceived a fire. Perhaps I will bring you from it a burning brand﴾, that is, a firebrand from the fire. In another verse: ﴿or a brand from the fire﴾ [Al-Qasas: 29], which is the ember that has a flame. ﴿So that you may warm yourselves﴾ [Al-Qasas: 29] indicates the presence of cold. His saying ﴿a burning brand﴾ indicates the presence of darkness.

* *

His saying ﴿or find at the fire some guidance﴾ means: someone who will guide me to the way. This indicates that he had strayed from the road, as al-Thawri said, from Abu Sa'd al-A'war, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿or find at the fire some guidance﴾: he said, "Someone who will guide me to the road." They were in winter and had lost the road. So when he saw the fire he said: "If I do not find anyone to guide me to the road, I will come to you with fire with which you may kindle a flame."

From this point onward, may He be blessed and exalted, He began to mention the story of Musa [upon him peace] [[Addition from MS F.]]: how the revelation came to him and how He spoke to him. This was after Musa had completed the term that was between him and his father-in-law in tending the sheep, and he set out with his family. It was said that he was heading for the land of Egypt, after his absence from it had lasted more than ten years, and his wife was with him. He lost his way. It was a wintry night. He halted at a place between ravines and mountains, in cold and winter, with clouds, darkness and fog. He began to strike a flint he had with him [[In MS F: "to him"]] in order to kindle a fire, as was his habit, but it produced no spark and nothing came out of it. While he was in this state, he perceived a fire from the side of the Tur, that is, a fire appeared to him from the side of the mountain there, on his right. So he said to his family, giving them good news: ﴿Indeed, I have perceived a fire. Perhaps I will bring you from it a burning brand﴾, that is, a firebrand from the fire. In another verse: ﴿or a brand from the fire﴾ [Al-Qasas: 29], which is the ember that has a flame. ﴿So that you may warm yourselves﴾ [Al-Qasas: 29] indicates the presence of cold. His saying ﴿a burning brand﴾ indicates the presence of darkness.

* *

His saying ﴿or find at the fire some guidance﴾ means: someone who will guide me to the way. This indicates that he had strayed from the road, as al-Thawri said, from Abu Sa'd al-A'war, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿or find at the fire some guidance﴾: he said, "Someone who will guide me to the road." They were in winter and had lost the road. So when he saw the fire he said: "If I do not find anyone to guide me to the road, I will come to you with fire with which you may kindle a flame."

يقول الله تعالى: ﴿فَلَمَّا أَتَاهَا﴾ أي: النار، واقترب منها، ﴿نُودِيَ يَا مُوسَى﴾. وفي الآية الأخرى: ﴿نُودِيَ مِنْ شَاطِئِ الْوَادِ الأيْمَنِ فِي الْبُقْعَةِ الْمُبَارَكَةِ مِنَ الشَّجَرَةِ أَنْ يَا مُوسَى إِنِّي أَنَا اللَّهُ﴾ [القصص: 30]. وقال هاهنا: ﴿إِنِّي أَنَا رَبُّكَ﴾ أي: الذي يكلمك ويخاطبك. ﴿فَاخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ﴾. قال علي بن أبي طالب، وأبو ذر، وأبو أيوب، وغير واحد من السلف: كانتا من جلد حمار غير مذكّى.

وقيل: إنما أمره بخلع نعليه تعظيمًا للبقعة.

قال سعيد بن جبير: كما يُؤمر الرجل أن يخلع نعليه إذا أراد دخول الكعبة.

وقيل: ليطأ الأرض المقدسة بقدميه حافيًا غير منتعل. وقيل غير ذلك، والله أعلم.

* *

وقوله: ﴿طُوًى﴾. قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: هو اسم للوادي.

وكذا قال غير واحد، وعلى هذا يكون عطف بيان (apposition، أي بدل يوضح المبدل منه).

وقيل: هو عبارة عن الأمر بالوطء بقدميه.

وقيل: لأنه قُدّس مرتين، وطوى له البركة وكُررت. والأول أصح، كقوله: ﴿إِذْ نَادَاهُ رَبُّهُ بِالْوَادِ الْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى﴾ [النازعات: 16].

* *

وقوله: ﴿وَأَنَا اخْتَرْتُكَ﴾ كقوله: ﴿إِنِّي اصْطَفَيْتُكَ عَلَى النَّاسِ بِرِسَالاتِي وَبِكَلامِي﴾ [الأعراف: 144]، أي: على جميع الناس الموجودين في زمانه.

وقد قيل: إن الله تعالى قال: يا موسى، أتدري لم خصصتك بالتكليم من بين الناس؟ قال: لا. قال: لأنه لم يتواضع لي أحد تواضعك.

* *

وقوله: ﴿فَاسْتَمِعْ لِمَا يُوحَى﴾ أي: اسمع الآن ما أقوله لك وأوحيه إليك.

﴿إِنَّنِي أَنَا اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلا أَنَا﴾. هذا أول واجب على المكلفين، أن يعلموا أنه لا إله إلا الله، وحده لا شريك له.

* *

وقوله: ﴿فَاعْبُدْنِي﴾ أي: وحّدني وأقم عبادتي من غير شريك. ﴿وَأَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ لِذِكْرِي﴾. قيل: معناه: صلِّ لتذكرني. وقيل: معناه: وأقم الصلاة عند ذكرك لي.

ويشهد للثاني ما قال الإمام أحمد: حدثنا عبد الرحمن بن مهدي، حدثنا المثنى بن سعيد، عن قتادة، عن أنس، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إذا رقد أحدكم عن الصلاة، أو غفل عنها، فليصلّها إذا ذكرها؛ فإن الله تعالى قال: ﴿وَأَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ لِذِكْرِي﴾".[[المسند (3/184).]]

وفي الصحيحين عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: "مَن نام عن صلاة أو نسيها، فكفارتها أن يصليها إذا ذكرها، لا كفارة لها إلا ذلك".[[صحيح البخاري برقم (597) وصحيح مسلم برقم (684).]]

* *

وقوله: ﴿إِنَّ السَّاعَةَ آتِيَةٌ﴾ أي: قائمة لا محالة، وكائنة لا بد منها.

* *

وقوله: ﴿أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا﴾. قال الضحاك، عن ابن عباس: إنه كان يقرؤها: "أكاد أخفيها من نفسي"، يقول: لأنها لا تخفى من نفس الله أبدًا.

وقال سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس: "من نفسه". وكذا قال مجاهد، وأبو صالح، ويحيى بن رافع.

وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: ﴿أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا﴾ يقول: لا أُطلع عليها أحدًا غيري.

وقال السدي: ليس أحد من أهل السماوات والأرض إلا قد أخفى الله عنه علم الساعة. وهي في قراءة ابن مسعود: "إني أكاد أخفيها من نفسي"، يقول: كتمتها عن الخلائق، حتى لو استطعت أن أكتمها من نفسي لفعلت.

وقال قتادة: ﴿أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا﴾ وهي في بعض القراءة: "أخفيها من نفسي"، ولعمري لقد أخفاها الله من الملائكة المقربين، ومن الأنبياء والمرسلين.

قلت: وهذا كقوله تعالى: ﴿قُلْ لَا يَعْلَمُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالأرْضِ الْغَيْبَ إِلا اللَّهُ﴾ [النمل: 65]، وقال: ﴿ثَقُلَتْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالأرْضِ لَا تَأْتِيكُمْ إِلا بَغْتَةً﴾ [الأعراف: 187]، أي: ثقل علمها على أهل السماوات والأرض.

وقال ابن أبي حاتم: حدثنا أبو زرعة، حدثنا منجاب، حدثنا أبو نُمَيلة، حدثني محمد بن سهل الأسدي، عن وقّاء قال: أقرأنيها سعيد بن جبير: (أَكَادُ أَخفيها)، يعني بنصب الألف وخفض الفاء، يقول: أُظهرها. ثم قال: أما سمعت قول الشاعر:

دأبَ شهرين، ثم شهرًا دميكًا ... بأريكَين يخفيان غميرًا ...

وقال الأسدي: الغمير: نبت رطب، ينبت في خلال يبس. والأريكين: موضع، والدميك: الشهر التام. وهذا الشعر لكعب بن زهير.

* *

وقوله سبحانه وتعالى: ﴿لِتُجْزَى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا تَسْعَى﴾ أي: أقيمها لا محالة، لأجزي كل عامل بعمله، ﴿فَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُ وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرًّا يَرَهُ﴾ [الزلزلة: 7، 8]، و﴿إِنَّمَا تُجْزَوْنَ مَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [الطور: 16].

* *

وقوله: ﴿فَلا يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنْهَا مَنْ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِهَا وَاتَّبَعَ هَوَاهُ فَتَرْدَى﴾. المراد بهذا الخطاب آحاد المكلفين، أي: لا تتبعوا سبيل من كذّب بالساعة، وأقبل على ملاذّه في دنياه، وعصى مولاه، واتبع هواه، فمن وافقهم على ذلك فقد خاب وخسر. ﴿فَتَرْدَى﴾ أي: تهلك وتعطب. قال الله تعالى: ﴿وَمَا يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مَالُهُ إِذَا تَرَدَّى﴾ [الليل: 11].

يقول الله تعالى: ﴿فَلَمَّا أَتَاهَا﴾ أي: النار، واقترب منها، ﴿نُودِيَ يَا مُوسَى﴾. وفي الآية الأخرى: ﴿نُودِيَ مِنْ شَاطِئِ الْوَادِ الأيْمَنِ فِي الْبُقْعَةِ الْمُبَارَكَةِ مِنَ الشَّجَرَةِ أَنْ يَا مُوسَى إِنِّي أَنَا اللَّهُ﴾ [القصص: 30]. وقال هاهنا: ﴿إِنِّي أَنَا رَبُّكَ﴾ أي: الذي يكلمك ويخاطبك. ﴿فَاخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ﴾. قال علي بن أبي طالب، وأبو ذر، وأبو أيوب، وغير واحد من السلف: كانتا من جلد حمار غير مذكّى.

وقيل: إنما أمره بخلع نعليه تعظيمًا للبقعة.

قال سعيد بن جبير: كما يُؤمر الرجل أن يخلع نعليه إذا أراد دخول الكعبة.

وقيل: ليطأ الأرض المقدسة بقدميه حافيًا غير منتعل. وقيل غير ذلك، والله أعلم.

وقوله: ﴿طُوًى﴾. قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: هو اسم للوادي.

وكذا قال غير واحد، وعلى هذا يكون عطف بيان (apposition، أي بدل يوضح المبدل منه).

وقيل: هو عبارة عن الأمر بالوطء بقدميه.

وقيل: لأنه قُدّس مرتين، وطوى له البركة وكُررت. والأول أصح، كقوله: ﴿إِذْ نَادَاهُ رَبُّهُ بِالْوَادِ الْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى﴾ [النازعات: 16].

* *

وقوله: ﴿وَأَنَا اخْتَرْتُكَ﴾ كقوله: ﴿إِنِّي اصْطَفَيْتُكَ عَلَى النَّاسِ بِرِسَالاتِي وَبِكَلامِي﴾ [الأعراف: 144]، أي: على جميع الناس الموجودين في زمانه.

وقد قيل: إن الله تعالى قال: يا موسى، أتدري لم خصصتك بالتكليم من بين الناس؟ قال: لا. قال: لأنه لم يتواضع لي أحد تواضعك.

* *

وقوله: ﴿فَاسْتَمِعْ لِمَا يُوحَى﴾ أي: اسمع الآن ما أقوله لك وأوحيه إليك.

﴿إِنَّنِي أَنَا اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلا أَنَا﴾. هذا أول واجب على المكلفين، أن يعلموا أنه لا إله إلا الله، وحده لا شريك له.

* *

وقوله: ﴿فَاعْبُدْنِي﴾ أي: وحّدني وأقم عبادتي من غير شريك. ﴿وَأَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ لِذِكْرِي﴾. قيل: معناه: صلِّ لتذكرني. وقيل: معناه: وأقم الصلاة عند ذكرك لي.

ويشهد للثاني ما قال الإمام أحمد: حدثنا عبد الرحمن بن مهدي، حدثنا المثنى بن سعيد، عن قتادة، عن أنس، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إذا رقد أحدكم عن الصلاة، أو غفل عنها، فليصلّها إذا ذكرها؛ فإن الله تعالى قال: ﴿وَأَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ لِذِكْرِي﴾".[[المسند (3/184).]]

وفي الصحيحين عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: "مَن نام عن صلاة أو نسيها، فكفارتها أن يصليها إذا ذكرها، لا كفارة لها إلا ذلك".[[صحيح البخاري برقم (597) وصحيح مسلم برقم (684).]]

* *

وقوله: ﴿إِنَّ السَّاعَةَ آتِيَةٌ﴾ أي: قائمة لا محالة، وكائنة لا بد منها.

* *

وقوله: ﴿أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا﴾. قال الضحاك، عن ابن عباس: إنه كان يقرؤها: "أكاد أخفيها من نفسي"، يقول: لأنها لا تخفى من نفس الله أبدًا.

وقال سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس: "من نفسه". وكذا قال مجاهد، وأبو صالح، ويحيى بن رافع.

وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: ﴿أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا﴾ يقول: لا أُطلع عليها أحدًا غيري.

وقال السدي: ليس أحد من أهل السماوات والأرض إلا قد أخفى الله عنه علم الساعة. وهي في قراءة ابن مسعود: "إني أكاد أخفيها من نفسي"، يقول: كتمتها عن الخلائق، حتى لو استطعت أن أكتمها من نفسي لفعلت.

وقال قتادة: ﴿أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا﴾ وهي في بعض القراءة: "أخفيها من نفسي"، ولعمري لقد أخفاها الله من الملائكة المقربين، ومن الأنبياء والمرسلين.

قلت: وهذا كقوله تعالى: ﴿قُلْ لَا يَعْلَمُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالأرْضِ الْغَيْبَ إِلا اللَّهُ﴾ [النمل: 65]، وقال: ﴿ثَقُلَتْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالأرْضِ لَا تَأْتِيكُمْ إِلا بَغْتَةً﴾ [الأعراف: 187]، أي: ثقل علمها على أهل السماوات والأرض.

وقال ابن أبي حاتم: حدثنا أبو زرعة، حدثنا منجاب، حدثنا أبو نُمَيلة، حدثني محمد بن سهل الأسدي، عن وقّاء قال: أقرأنيها سعيد بن جبير: (أَكَادُ أَخفيها)، يعني بنصب الألف وخفض الفاء، يقول: أُظهرها. ثم قال: أما سمعت قول الشاعر:

دأبَ شهرين، ثم شهرًا دميكًا ... بأريكَين يخفيان غميرًا ...

وقال الأسدي: الغمير: نبت رطب، ينبت في خلال يبس. والأريكين: موضع، والدميك: الشهر التام. وهذا الشعر لكعب بن زهير.

* *

وقوله سبحانه وتعالى: ﴿لِتُجْزَى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا تَسْعَى﴾ أي: أقيمها لا محالة، لأجزي كل عامل بعمله، ﴿فَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُ وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرًّا يَرَهُ﴾ [الزلزلة: 7، 8]، و﴿إِنَّمَا تُجْزَوْنَ مَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [الطور: 16].

* *

وقوله: ﴿فَلا يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنْهَا مَنْ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِهَا وَاتَّبَعَ هَوَاهُ فَتَرْدَى﴾. المراد بهذا الخطاب آحاد المكلفين، أي: لا تتبعوا سبيل من كذّب بالساعة، وأقبل على ملاذّه في دنياه، وعصى مولاه، واتبع هواه، فمن وافقهم على ذلك فقد خاب وخسر. ﴿فَتَرْدَى﴾ أي: تهلك وتعطب. قال الله تعالى: ﴿وَمَا يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مَالُهُ إِذَا تَرَدَّى﴾ [الليل: 11].

يقول الله تعالى: ﴿فَلَمَّا أَتَاهَا﴾ أي: النار، واقترب منها، ﴿نُودِيَ يَا مُوسَى﴾. وفي الآية الأخرى: ﴿نُودِيَ مِنْ شَاطِئِ الْوَادِ الأيْمَنِ فِي الْبُقْعَةِ الْمُبَارَكَةِ مِنَ الشَّجَرَةِ أَنْ يَا مُوسَى إِنِّي أَنَا اللَّهُ﴾ [القصص: 30]. وقال هاهنا: ﴿إِنِّي أَنَا رَبُّكَ﴾ أي: الذي يكلمك ويخاطبك. ﴿فَاخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ﴾. قال علي بن أبي طالب، وأبو ذر، وأبو أيوب، وغير واحد من السلف: كانتا من جلد حمار غير مذكّى.

وقيل: إنما أمره بخلع نعليه تعظيمًا للبقعة.

قال سعيد بن جبير: كما يُؤمر الرجل أن يخلع نعليه إذا أراد دخول الكعبة.

وقيل: ليطأ الأرض المقدسة بقدميه حافيًا غير منتعل. وقيل غير ذلك، والله أعلم.

وقال سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس: "من نفسه". وكذا قال مجاهد، وأبو صالح، ويحيى بن رافع.

وقال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: ﴿أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا﴾ يقول: لا أُطلع عليها أحدًا غيري.

وقال السدي: ليس أحد من أهل السماوات والأرض إلا قد أخفى الله عنه علم الساعة. وهي في قراءة ابن مسعود: "إني أكاد أخفيها من نفسي"، يقول: كتمتها عن الخلائق، حتى لو استطعت أن أكتمها من نفسي لفعلت.

وقال قتادة: ﴿أَكَادُ أُخْفِيهَا﴾ وهي في بعض القراءة: "أخفيها من نفسي"، ولعمري لقد أخفاها الله من الملائكة المقربين، ومن الأنبياء والمرسلين.

قلت: وهذا كقوله تعالى: ﴿قُلْ لَا يَعْلَمُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالأرْضِ الْغَيْبَ إِلا اللَّهُ﴾ [النمل: 65]، وقال: ﴿ثَقُلَتْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالأرْضِ لَا تَأْتِيكُمْ إِلا بَغْتَةً﴾ [الأعراف: 187]، أي: ثقل علمها على أهل السماوات والأرض.

وقال ابن أبي حاتم: حدثنا أبو زرعة، حدثنا منجاب، حدثنا أبو نُمَيلة، حدثني محمد بن سهل الأسدي، عن وقّاء قال: أقرأنيها سعيد بن جبير: (أَكَادُ أَخفيها)، يعني بنصب الألف وخفض الفاء، يقول: أُظهرها. ثم قال: أما سمعت قول الشاعر:

دأبَ شهرين، ثم شهرًا دميكًا ... بأريكَين يخفيان غميرًا ...

وقال الأسدي: الغمير: نبت رطب، ينبت في خلال يبس. والأريكين: موضع، والدميك: الشهر التام. وهذا الشعر لكعب بن زهير.

وقوله سبحانه وتعالى: ﴿لِتُجْزَى كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِمَا تَسْعَى﴾ أي: أقيمها لا محالة، لأجزي كل عامل بعمله، ﴿فَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ خَيْرًا يَرَهُ وَمَنْ يَعْمَلْ مِثْقَالَ ذَرَّةٍ شَرًّا يَرَهُ﴾ [الزلزلة: 7، 8]، و﴿إِنَّمَا تُجْزَوْنَ مَا كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ [الطور: 16].

* *

وقوله: ﴿فَلا يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنْهَا مَنْ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِهَا وَاتَّبَعَ هَوَاهُ فَتَرْدَى﴾. المراد بهذا الخطاب آحاد المكلفين، أي: لا تتبعوا سبيل من كذّب بالساعة، وأقبل على ملاذّه في دنياه، وعصى مولاه، واتبع هواه، فمن وافقهم على ذلك فقد خاب وخسر. ﴿فَتَرْدَى﴾ أي: تهلك وتعطب. قال الله تعالى: ﴿وَمَا يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مَالُهُ إِذَا تَرَدَّى﴾ [الليل: 11].

يقول الله تعالى: ﴿فَلَمَّا أَتَاهَا﴾ أي: النار، واقترب منها، ﴿نُودِيَ يَا مُوسَى﴾. وفي الآية الأخرى: ﴿نُودِيَ مِنْ شَاطِئِ الْوَادِ الأيْمَنِ فِي الْبُقْعَةِ الْمُبَارَكَةِ مِنَ الشَّجَرَةِ أَنْ يَا مُوسَى إِنِّي أَنَا اللَّهُ﴾ [القصص: 30]. وقال هاهنا: ﴿إِنِّي أَنَا رَبُّكَ﴾ أي: الذي يكلمك ويخاطبك. ﴿فَاخْلَعْ نَعْلَيْكَ﴾. قال علي بن أبي طالب، وأبو ذر، وأبو أيوب، وغير واحد من السلف: كانتا من جلد حمار غير مذكّى.

وقيل: إنما أمره بخلع نعليه تعظيمًا للبقعة.

قال سعيد بن جبير: كما يُؤمر الرجل أن يخلع نعليه إذا أراد دخول الكعبة.

وقيل: ليطأ الأرض المقدسة بقدميه حافيًا غير منتعل. وقيل غير ذلك، والله أعلم.

وقوله: ﴿طُوًى﴾. قال علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: هو اسم للوادي.

وكذا قال غير واحد، وعلى هذا يكون عطف بيان (apposition، أي بدل يوضح المبدل منه).

وقيل: هو عبارة عن الأمر بالوطء بقدميه.

وقيل: لأنه قُدّس مرتين، وطوى له البركة وكُررت. والأول أصح، كقوله: ﴿إِذْ نَادَاهُ رَبُّهُ بِالْوَادِ الْمُقَدَّسِ طُوًى﴾ [النازعات: 16].

* *

وقوله: ﴿وَأَنَا اخْتَرْتُكَ﴾ كقوله: ﴿إِنِّي اصْطَفَيْتُكَ عَلَى النَّاسِ بِرِسَالاتِي وَبِكَلامِي﴾ [الأعراف: 144]، أي: على جميع الناس الموجودين في زمانه.

وقد قيل: إن الله تعالى قال: يا موسى، أتدري لم خصصتك بالتكليم من بين الناس؟ قال: لا. قال: لأنه لم يتواضع لي أحد تواضعك.

* *

وقوله: ﴿فَاسْتَمِعْ لِمَا يُوحَى﴾ أي: اسمع الآن ما أقوله لك وأوحيه إليك.

﴿إِنَّنِي أَنَا اللَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلا أَنَا﴾. هذا أول واجب على المكلفين، أن يعلموا أنه لا إله إلا الله، وحده لا شريك له.

* *

وقوله: ﴿فَاعْبُدْنِي﴾ أي: وحّدني وأقم عبادتي من غير شريك. ﴿وَأَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ لِذِكْرِي﴾. قيل: معناه: صلِّ لتذكرني. وقيل: معناه: وأقم الصلاة عند ذكرك لي.

ويشهد للثاني ما قال الإمام أحمد: حدثنا عبد الرحمن بن مهدي، حدثنا المثنى بن سعيد، عن قتادة، عن أنس، عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "إذا رقد أحدكم عن الصلاة، أو غفل عنها، فليصلّها إذا ذكرها؛ فإن الله تعالى قال: ﴿وَأَقِمِ الصَّلاةَ لِذِكْرِي﴾".[[المسند (3/184).]]

وفي الصحيحين عن أنس قال: قال رسول الله ﷺ: "مَن نام عن صلاة أو نسيها، فكفارتها أن يصليها إذا ذكرها، لا كفارة لها إلا ذلك".[[صحيح البخاري برقم (597) وصحيح مسلم برقم (684).]]

وقوله: ﴿فَلا يَصُدَّنَّكَ عَنْهَا مَنْ لَا يُؤْمِنُ بِهَا وَاتَّبَعَ هَوَاهُ فَتَرْدَى﴾. المراد بهذا الخطاب آحاد المكلفين، أي: لا تتبعوا سبيل من كذّب بالساعة، وأقبل على ملاذّه في دنياه، وعصى مولاه، واتبع هواه، فمن وافقهم على ذلك فقد خاب وخسر. ﴿فَتَرْدَى﴾ أي: تهلك وتعطب. قال الله تعالى: ﴿وَمَا يُغْنِي عَنْهُ مَالُهُ إِذَا تَرَدَّى﴾ [الليل: 11].

This is a proof from God, Exalted is He, given to Musa, peace be upon him, and a great miracle and a striking departure from the ordinary course of things. It shows that no one can produce the like of it except Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and that it is brought only by a sent Prophet. As for His saying: ﴿And what is that in your right hand, O Musa?﴾, some of the commentators (mufassirun) said: He said this to him only to put him at ease. It was also said: He said it as a confirmation, meaning: As for this thing in your right hand, it is your staff, which you know; you will see what We do with it now. ﴿And what is that in your right hand, O Musa?﴾ is a question asked for confirmation.

﴿He said: It is my staff. I lean upon it,﴾ that is, I rely on it while walking, ﴿and I beat down [leaves] with it for my sheep,﴾ that is, I strike the tree with it so that its leaves fall, for my sheep to graze on.

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim said, from Imam Malik: The hashsh (beating down leaves) is when a man places the mihjan (crook) on the branch and then shakes it until its leaves and fruit fall, without breaking the stick. This is hashsh, and it is not khabt (beating violently). Maymun ibn Mihran also said the same.

* *

His saying: ﴿and I have in it other uses (ma'arib)﴾ means: benefits, advantages and other needs beyond that. Some of them have strained to name some of those uses that were left unspecified. It was said: it would give him light at night, guard his sheep while he slept, and he would plant it and it would become a tree that shades him, and other extraordinary things beyond the ordinary course.

The apparent meaning is that it was not like that. Had it been so, Musa would not have been alarmed at its turning into a serpent, and he would not have fled from it in flight. It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: Its name was Masha. And Allah knows best what is correct.

Then he was called a second time: "Take it and do not fear." Then in the third call it was said to him: "You are among the secure," and he took it.

Wahb ibn Munabbih, concerning His saying: ﴿So he cast it, and behold, it was a serpent, moving swiftly﴾, said: He cast it on the surface of the earth, and then in an instant there was the greatest serpent that those who looked had ever seen. It passed by a rock like a female camel in heat and swallowed it, and it struck with one of its fangs at the root of a great tree and uprooted it. Its eyes blazed like fire, and the crook had turned into a mane. It was said: its hair was like shooting stars, and its two forks had become like a wide well, with molars and fangs in it, and it made a grinding sound. When Musa saw this, he turned and fled without looking back, and he went on until he was far away. He thought that he had overpowered the serpent. Then he remembered his Lord and stopped out of shame before Him. Then he was called: "O Musa, return to where you were." Musa returned, and he was in great fear. He was told: ﴿Take it﴾ with your right hand, ﴿and do not fear; We will return it to its original condition﴾. Musa was then wearing a woolen garment, and he thrust into it with some wooden sticks. When He commanded him to take it, he let the edge of the garment fall over his hand. An angel said to him: "Tell me, O Musa, if Allah permitted what you fear, would the garment avail you anything?" He said: "No, but I am weak, and I was created weak." He then uncovered his hand and placed it on the mouth of the serpent until he heard the sound of its molars and fangs. Then he gripped it, and behold, it was his staff that he knew, and his hand was in the place where he used to place it when he leaned, between the two forks. Therefore He, Exalted is He, said: ﴿We will return it to its original condition﴾, that is, to its state known before that.

This is a second proof given to Musa, peace be upon him: Allah commanded him to put his hand into his collar, as He stated explicitly in another verse, and here He expressed this by His words: ﴿Draw your hand close to your side﴾. He said in another place: ﴿And draw your arm close to you against fear. These are two proofs from your Lord to Pharaoh and his chiefs﴾ [al-Qasas: 32].

Mujahid said: ﴿Draw your hand close to your side﴾ means his palm beneath his armpit.

That was because when Musa put his hand into his collar and then took it out, it would come out shining, like a piece of the moon.

Say to him: Answer your Lord, for He is vast in forgiveness, and He has granted you respite for four hundred years, during all of which you have been waging war against Him, reviling Him, making images of Him, and turning His servants from His path, while He sends down rain upon you from the sky and makes the earth grow for you; you have not fallen ill, nor grown old, nor become poor, nor been overcome. Had Allah wished to hasten punishment for you, He would have done so, but He is patient and of great forbearance. Strive against him with yourself and your brother, and you two intend by your striving against him; for if I wished to bring against him armies he could not withstand, I would do so. But I want this weak servant, whom his own self and his multitudes have made conceited, to know that a small group, and there is no smallness with Me, overcomes a large group by My permission. I am the swiftest of all to support My friends. Does the one who wars against Me think he can withstand Me? Or does the one who opposes Me think he can overpower Me? Or does the one who contends with Me think he can outrun or escape Me? How could that be, when I am the one who avenges them in this world and the Hereafter, and I do not leave those in need among them to anyone other than Me.

By My right, I am the Self-Sufficient; there is no self-sufficiency other than Mine. So convey My message to him, call him to My worship, My oneness, and sincerity to Me, remind him of My days, warn him of My vengeance and My might, and inform him that nothing can stand against My anger. Speak to him between these matters with gentle speech, perhaps he will remember or fear. And inform him that I am quicker to pardon and forgive than to anger and punish. Let not what I have granted him of the garments of this world alarm you, for his forelock is in My hand; he does not speak, blink, or breathe except by My permission. Say to him: Answer your Lord, for He is vast in forgiveness, and He has granted you respite for four hundred years, during all of which you have been waging war against Him, reviling Him, making images of Him, and turning His servants from His path, while He sends down rain upon you from the sky and makes the earth grow for you; you have not fallen ill, nor grown old, nor become poor, nor been overcome. But I want this weak servant, whom his own self and his multitudes have made conceited, to know that a small group, and there is no smallness with Me, overcomes a large group by My permission. Or does the one who contends with Me think he can outrun or escape Me? How could that be, when I am the one who avenges them in this world and the Hereafter, and I do not leave those in need among them to anyone other than Me.

His words: ﴿Indeed You have been, of us, Seeing﴾ mean: in Your choosing us, Your giving us prophethood, and Your sending us to Your enemy Pharaoh; so to You is praise for that.

This is an answer from Allah to His Messenger Musa, peace be upon him, regarding what he asked of his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, and a reminder to him of the past blessings He bestowed upon him, such as the inspiration He gave his mother while she was nursing him and was afraid for him from Pharaoh and his chiefs, that they would kill him. This was because he had been born in the year in which they were killing the boys. So she made him an ark (tabut), and she would nurse him, then place him in it and send it onto the river, which is the Nile, and she would hold it by a rope to her house. Once she went to tie it, but it slipped from her and the river carried it away. She was thereby struck with the grief and anguish that Allah mentioned about her in His saying: ﴿And the heart of the mother of Musa became empty. She was about to disclose him, had We not strengthened her heart so she would be of the believers﴾ [Al-Qasas: 10]. The river carried him to the house of Pharaoh, ﴿and the family of Pharaoh picked him up to be to them an enemy and a grief﴾ [Al-Qasas: 8], meaning a decree decreed by Allah, since they were the ones killing the boys of the Children of Israel out of fear of the existence of Musa. Allah, to whom belongs the great authority and complete power, decreed that he would be raised only on the bed of Pharaoh, and be nourished with his food and drink, along with Pharaoh's and his wife's love for him. Therefore He said: ﴿He will take him, My enemy and his enemy. And I bestowed upon you love from Me﴾ [meaning: among your enemy, I made him love you. Salamah ibn Kuhayl said regarding ﴿And I bestowed upon you love from Me﴾: "He said: I made you beloved to My servants."]

﴿And that you may be brought up under My eye﴾. Abu 'Imran al-Jawni said: "You would be raised under the eye of Allah."
Qatadah said: "You would be nourished under My eye."
Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna said: "﴿And that you may be brought up under My eye﴾: in a manner where I see."
'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "That is, I would make him in the house of the king, enjoying blessings and luxury, his food with them being the food of the king. That is the making (sun'ah)."

* *

His saying: ﴿When your sister walked and said, "Shall I direct you to one who will be responsible for him?" So We returned you to your mother that her eye might be comforted and not grieve﴾. This is because, when he settled with the family of Pharaoh, they offered him wet nurses, but he refused them. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And We had prohibited to him the wet nurses before﴾. So his sister came and said: ﴿Shall I direct you to a household who will raise him for you, and they will be sincere to him?﴾ [Al-Qasas: 12]. She meant: "Shall I direct you to one who will nurse him for you in exchange for a wage?" So she went with him, and they with her, to his mother, and she offered her breast to him, and he accepted it. They rejoiced greatly at that and hired her to nurse him. Thereby she gained happiness, elevation and comfort in this world and in the Hereafter, which is more abundant and more generous. Therefore it has come in a hadith: "The example of the craftsman who seeks reward in his craft for good is like the mother of Musa, who nurses her child and takes her wage." [Abu Dawud related it in al-Marasil, no. 332, through the route of Jubayr ibn Nufayr, similarly, and its wording is: "The example of those among my nation who fight and take the reward, and strengthen themselves against their enemy by it, is like the mother of Musa, who nurses her child and takes her wage."]

And the Most High said here: ﴿So We returned you to your mother that her eye might be comforted and not grieve﴾, meaning: over you. ﴿And you killed a soul﴾, meaning the Copt. ﴿And We delivered you from distress﴾, which is what befell him because of the determination of the family of Pharaoh to kill him, so he fled from them, running away, until he reached the water of Madyan. And that righteous man said to him: ﴿Fear not. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people﴾ [Al-Qasas: 25].

* *

His saying: ﴿And We tried you with a [severe] trial﴾. Imam Abu 'Abd al-Rahman Ahmad ibn Shu'ayb al-Nasa'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said in the Book of Tafsir in his Sunan, regarding His saying: ﴿And We tried you with a [severe] trial﴾: The hadith of the trials (al-futun):

Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Asbagh ibn Zayd informed us, al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Jubayr informed me, who said: I asked Abdullah ibn 'Abbas about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to Musa, peace be upon him: ﴿And We tried you with a [severe] trial﴾, and I asked him what al-futun is. He said: "Resume the day, O son of Jubayr, for it has a long story." When I woke in the morning, I went to Ibn 'Abbas to fulfil from him what he had promised me of the hadith of the trials. He said: "Pharaoh and his companions discussed what Allah had promised Ibrahim, peace be upon him, that He would place in his descendants prophets and kings. Some of them said: 'The Children of Israel are awaiting that, and they have no doubt about it, and they thought it was Yusuf ibn Ya'qub.' When he died they said: 'That was not the promise of Ibrahim.' Pharaoh said: 'So how do you see it?' They conferred and agreed on a plan to send men with them carrying knives, going around among the Children of Israel, so that they would not find any male newborn without slaughtering him. They did so. When they saw that the elders of the Children of Israel were dying by their appointed times while the young were being slaughtered, they said: 'Soon you will destroy the Children of Israel, and you will come to be engaged in the work and service that they used to perform for you. So kill every male newborn in one year, and leave a year without killing any of them, so that the young will grow to replace those of the elders who die. For they will not increase in number by those you spare and fear their outnumbering you, nor will they be destroyed by those you kill and need them.' So they agreed on that."

Umm Musa conceived Harun in the year in which the boys were not slaughtered, and she gave birth to him openly and safely. When the following year came, she conceived Musa, peace be upon him, and anxiety and sorrow fell into her heart. That was of the trials, O son of Jubayr, that entered upon him in his mother's womb, of what was intended for him. Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, inspired to her that ﴿Do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers﴾ [Al-Qasas: 7]. He commanded her, when she gave birth, to place him in an ark and then throw him into the river (al-yamm). When she gave birth she did so, and when her son disappeared from her, Satan came to her and she said to herself: "What has become of my son? If he had been slaughtered before me, I would have buried him and shrouded him, and that would be more beloved to me than throwing him to the creatures and fish of the sea."

The water carried him until it brought him to the landing place of the water-drawing of Pharaoh's wife's maidservants. When they saw him, they took him and wanted to open the ark. Some of them said: "In this is wealth. If we open it, the queen will not believe us about what we found in it." So they carried it as it was, without taking anything out of it, until they lifted it to her. When she opened it she saw a boy, and there was cast upon him from her a love such as had never been cast upon anyone else. The heart of Umm Musa became empty of the remembrance of everything except the remembrance of Musa.

When the slaughterers heard of his matter, they came with their knives to the wife of Pharaoh to slaughter him. That was from the trials, O son of Jubayr. She said to them: "Leave him, for this one will not increase the Children of Israel. Until I go to Pharaoh and ask him to grant him to me. If he grants him to me, you will have done well and fairly, and if he orders his slaughter, I will not blame you."

She went to Pharaoh and said: ﴿The comfort of the eye for me and for you﴾ [Al-Qasas: 9]. Pharaoh said: "He will be yours, but as for me, I have no need of him." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, if Pharaoh had agreed that he would be a comfort of the eye for him as his wife did, Allah would have guided him as He guided her, but Allah deprived him of that." She sent to those around her, to every woman who had milk, to choose a wet nurse for him. Whenever a woman took him to nurse him, he would not turn to her breast, until the wife of Pharaoh feared that he would refuse milk and die. That saddened her, so she ordered him to be taken out to the market and the gathering of people, hoping to find a wet nurse from whom he would take. But he did not accept. Umm Musa became distraught, and she said to his sister: "Follow his trail and search for him, and see if you hear any mention of him, is my son alive or have the beasts eaten him?" She forgot what Allah had promised her. His sister saw him from afar while they did not notice, (al-junub: that a person's sight reaches a distant thing while it is beside him and he does not notice it). She said, out of joy, when the nurses had exhausted them: "I will direct you to a household who will raise him for you, and they will be sincere to him." They took her and said: "How do you know? What is their sincerity to him? Do they know him?" until they doubted in that, and that was from the trials, O son of Jubayr. She said: "Their sincerity to him and their compassion for him is their desire for the king's nursing and their hope for the king's benefit." They sent her, and she went to her mother and informed her of the news. His mother came, and when she placed him in her lap, he lunged at her breast and sucked it until his sides were filled with satisfaction. The messengers went to the wife of Pharaoh, giving her good news that we have found a wet nurse for your son. She sent for her. They brought her and him, and when she saw how he behaved with her, she said: "Stay and nurse my son, for I have never loved anything as I love him." Umm Musa said: "I cannot leave my house and my child to be lost. If you are content to give him to me, I will take him to my house, and he will be with me, and I will not neglect him in goodness [if you do, and if not], for I will not leave my house and my child." Umm Musa remembered what Allah had promised her, so she refused the wife of Pharaoh, and she was certain that Allah would fulfil His promise. She returned with him to her house that same day, and Allah made him grow well and preserved him for what He had decreed concerning him.

The Children of Israel remained in the outskirts of the town, refusing forced labour and oppression as much as they could. When Musa grew up, Pharaoh's wife said to Musa's mother: "Will you let me see my son?" So she promised her a day on which she would show him to her. Pharaoh's wife also said to her treasurers, her wet-nurses and her stewards: "None of you should fail to meet my son today with a gift and an honour, so that I may see that. And I am sending a trustworthy agent to count what each of you does." The gifts, the gratuities and the honours continued to greet him from the moment he left his mother's house until he entered Pharaoh's wife's presence. When he entered upon her, she gave him gifts, honoured him and rejoiced in him, and she rewarded his mother for the good care she had given him. Then she said: "I will bring him to Pharaoh so that he may give him gifts and honour him." When she brought him in to Pharaoh, Pharaoh placed him in his lap. Musa took hold of Pharaoh's beard and pulled it down towards the ground. The deluded enemies of Allah said to Pharaoh: "Do you not see what Allah promised Ibrahim, His prophet? He claimed that he would inherit you, overcome you and throw you down." So Pharaoh sent for the slaughterers to kill him. This was one of the trials, O Ibn Jubayr, after every affliction with which he was tested, and it was intended for him as a trial.

Then Pharaoh's wife came and said: "What has become of you regarding this boy whom you gave to me?" Pharaoh said: "Do you not see that he claims he will throw me down and overcome me?" She said: "Set between me and you a matter by which the truth will be known. Bring two embers and two pearls, and bring them near to him. If he reaches for the pearls and avoids the embers, then you will know that he understands. But if he takes the embers and does not want the pearls, you will know that no one who understands would prefer the embers over the pearls." So they brought them near to him, and he took the embers. Pharaoh snatched them from him, fearing that they would burn his hand. Pharaoh's wife said: "Do you not see?" Then Allah turned him away from them after he had intended to harm him, and Allah accomplishes His command.

When he reached his maturity and became a man, none of Pharaoh's household could approach any of the Children of Israel with oppression or forced labour while he was with them, until they withdrew entirely. One day, while Musa, peace be upon him, was walking in the outskirts of the city, he came upon two men fighting, one of them from Pharaoh's people and the other from the Children of Israel. The Israelite called on him for help against the Egyptian, so Musa became exceedingly angry, because he had struck him while knowing his standing among the Children of Israel and his protection of them. People did not know anything except that this was from the nursing, except Musa's mother, unless Allah (Subhanahu) had informed Musa of something about it that He had not informed anyone else. So Musa struck the Egyptian and killed him, and no one saw the two of them except Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the Israelite. When Musa killed the man, he said: ﴿This is from the work of Satan. Indeed, he is a clear, misleading enemy﴾ [al-Qasas: 15]. Then he said: ﴿My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me.﴾ So He forgave him. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful [al-Qasas: 16]. He woke in the city fearful, awaiting news. Then he went to Pharaoh, and it was said to him: "The Children of Israel have killed a man from the household of Pharaoh, so take our right and do not show them leniency." Pharaoh said: "Find me his killer and whoever will testify against him, for the king, even if he inclines towards his own people, cannot properly exact retribution without evidence and proof. So seek out for me the knowledge of this, and I will take your right for you." While they were searching and could not find any proof, behold, on the following day Musa saw that Israelite fighting another man from Pharaoh's household. The Israelite called on him for help against the Egyptian. Musa encountered him, regretting what he had done and disliking what he had seen. The Israelite became angry, wanting to strike the Egyptian. So Musa said to the Israelite, because of what he had done yesterday and today: ﴿Indeed, you are a clear transgressor﴾. The Israelite looked at Musa after he had said what he said, and saw that he was angry, just as he had been angry the day before when he killed the Egyptian. He feared that, after he had said to him, ﴿Indeed, you are a clear transgressor﴾ [al-Qasas: 18], Musa intended to strike him, when in fact he did not intend that but intended the Egyptian. The Israelite became afraid and said: ﴿O Musa, do you intend to kill me as you killed a soul yesterday?﴾ [al-Qasas: 19]. He said this only out of fear that Musa intended to kill him. So they parted, and the Egyptian went and informed them of what he had heard from the Israelite of the report when he said: ﴿Do you intend to kill me as you killed a soul yesterday?﴾ Then Pharaoh sent the slaughterers to kill Musa. But Musa took the main road, walking calmly, seeking Musa, while they did not fear that he would escape them. Then a man from the followers of Musa came from the farthest part of the city, took a shortcut and got ahead of them to Musa, and informed him of the news. This too was a trial, O Ibn Jubayr.

So Musa left, heading towards Madyan. He had not encountered any affliction before that, and he had no knowledge of the way except his good opinion of his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. He said: ﴿Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way﴾. When he arrived at the water of Madyan, he found a community of people watering their flocks, and besides them he found two women holding back [their flocks] [al-Qasas: 22–23].

That is, the two women were holding back their sheep. He said to them: "What is your business? Why do you stay apart and not water with the people?" They said: "We have no strength to compete with the people; we only wait for what is left over of their watering troughs." So he watered for them, drawing a great deal of water in the bucket until he was the first of the shepherds. The two women returned to their father with their sheep, and Musa, peace be upon him, withdrew and sat in the shade of a tree, and said: ﴿My Lord, indeed I am in need of whatever good You send down to me﴾ [al-Qasas: 24]. Their father was surprised at how quickly they returned with their sheep, full-uddered and well-fed, and he said: "You have something unusual today." They informed him of what Musa had done. So he commanded one of them to call him, and she went to Musa and called him. When he spoke with him, he said: ﴿Do not fear; you have escaped from the wrongdoing people﴾ [al-Qasas: 25]. Pharaoh and his people have no authority over us, and we are not in his kingdom. One of the two women said: ﴿O my father, hire him; indeed the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy﴾ [al-Qasas: 26]. Jealousy overcame him so that he said to her: "What do you know of his strength? And of his trustworthiness?" She said: "As for his strength, I saw from him, in the bucket when he watered for us, that I had never seen a man stronger in that watering than him. As for his trustworthiness, he looked at me when I approached him and walked towards him. When he knew that I was a woman, he lowered his head and did not raise it until I had conveyed your message to him. Then he said to me: 'Walk behind me and direct me to the way.' He would not have done this unless he was trustworthy." So her father was relieved and believed her, and he thought well of him what she had said.

He said to him: ﴿Would you like me to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine on condition that you serve me for eight years? And if you complete ten, then it is from you. I do not want to burden you. You will find me, if Allah wills, among the righteous﴾ [al-Qasas: 27]. He agreed, so it was incumbent upon the prophet of Allah, Musa, to serve for eight years, and two years were a favour from him. Allah fulfilled his obligation on his behalf, and so he completed ten.

Sa'id (that is, Ibn Jubayr) said: A man from among the Christians, one of their scholars, met me and said: "Do you know which of the two terms Musa fulfilled?" I said: "No," and at that time I did not know. Then I met Ibn 'Abbas and mentioned this to him. He said: "Do you not know that eight years were obligatory upon the prophet of Allah? It was not for the prophet of Allah to reduce any of it, and he knew that Allah would fulfil on Musa's behalf the term He had promised him, so he fulfilled ten years." Then I met the Christian and informed him of that. He said: "The one you asked, who informed you, knows better than you about that." I said: "Indeed, and more deserving [of knowing it]."

When Musa travelled with his family, there occurred the matter of the fire, the staff and his hand, which Allah related to you in the Qur'an. He complained to Allah, exalted is He, about what he feared from the household of Pharaoh regarding the man he had killed, and about the knot in his tongue, for there was a knot in his tongue that prevented him from much speech. He asked his Lord to help him through his brother Harun, to be a supporter for him and to speak on his behalf about much that his tongue could not express clearly. Allah granted him his request, loosened the knot in his tongue, and revealed to Harun, commanding him to meet him. So Musa set off with his staff until he met Harun, peace be upon them both. Then they both set out to Pharaoh and stood at his door for a while without being admitted. Then he admitted them after a severe barrier, and they said: ﴿Indeed, we are two messengers of your Lord﴾ [Ta-Ha: 47]. He said: "Who is your Lord?" They informed him of what Allah related to you in the Qur'an. He said: "What do you want?" They reminded him of the slain man, and he excused himself with what you have heard. He said: "I want you to believe in Allah and to send the Children of Israel with me." He refused him and said: ﴿So bring a sign, if you are among the truthful﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 154]. Then he threw his staff, and behold, it became a huge, swiftly moving serpent with its mouth wide open, rushing towards Pharaoh. When Pharaoh saw it approaching him, he feared it, leapt from his throne and called upon Musa to hold it back from him. Musa did so. Then he took his hand out of his garment, and it appeared white without any defect, meaning without leprosy. Then he returned it, and it went back to its former colour. Pharaoh consulted the chiefs around him about what he had seen. They said to him: ﴿These two are sorcerers who want to drive you out of your land with their sorcery and do away with your most exemplary way of life﴾ [Ta-Ha: 63], meaning their kingdom in which they were living, and their livelihood. They refused to give Musa anything of what he requested, and they said to him: "Gather the sorcerers, for they are many in your land, so that you may overcome their sorcery with your sorcery." So he sent to the cities, and every sorcerer who was learned in magic was gathered for him. When they came to Pharaoh, they said: "What does this sorcerer do?" They said: "He works with serpents." They said: "By Allah, no one on earth works with sorcery of serpents, ropes and staves as we do. What will be our reward if we overcome him?" He said to them: "You are my relatives and my close associates, and I will do for you everything you desire." So they agreed upon the day of the adornment, and that the people should be gathered in the forenoon.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Ibn 'Abbas told me that the day of the adornment on which Allah made Musa prevail over Pharaoh and the sorcerers was the day of 'Ashura (the tenth of Muharram).

When they gathered at one place, the people said to one another: "Come, let us attend this affair, ﴿so that we may follow the sorcerers, if they are the victors﴾" [Ash-Shu'ara: 40]. They meant Musa and Harun, mocking them. Then they said, "O Musa, ﴿either you throw, or we will be the ones who throw﴾" [Al-A'raf: 115], trusting in their own power through their sorcery. ﴿He said, "Rather, you throw"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 66]. ﴿So they threw their ropes and their staffs, and said, "By the might of Pharaoh, we are indeed the victors"﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 44]. Musa saw from their sorcery what made him feel fear within himself. So Allah revealed to him, "Throw your staff." When he threw it, it became a great serpent, its mouth wide open. The staffs began to entwine with the ropes until they became food for the serpent, entering into it, until it left no staff or rope [in one version: "rope"] unswallowed. When the sorcerers realized this, they said, "If this were sorcery, it would not have reached this extent of our sorcery. Rather, it is a command from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. We believe in Allah and in what Musa has brought, and we repent to Allah of what we were upon." So Allah broke the back of Pharaoh in that place, and [broke] his followers, and the truth became manifest, and what they had been doing was nullified. ﴿So they were defeated there and returned in humiliation﴾ [Al-A'raf: 119]. Pharaoh's wife was openly present, in humble attire, calling upon Allah for victory for Musa over Pharaoh and his followers. Whoever among Pharaoh's family saw her thought that she had only humbled herself out of compassion for Pharaoh and his followers, but her grief and concern were for Musa.

When Musa's stay was prolonged with Pharaoh's false promises, every time he brought a sign, Pharaoh promised him at that point that he would send the Children of Israel with him. But once it passed, he broke his promise and said, "Can your Lord produce anything other than this?" So Allah sent upon his people the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood as distinct signs. Each time, [Pharaoh] complained to Musa and asked him to remove it from him, and he made a covenant with him that he would send the Children of Israel with him. But once it was removed, he broke his promise and violated his covenant.

Until Allah commanded Musa to depart with his people, so he set out with them at night. When Pharaoh awoke in the morning and saw that they had gone, he sent [messengers] to the cities to gather [people], and he pursued them with a great and numerous army. Allah revealed to the sea: "When My servant Musa strikes you with his staff, split into twelve paths, so that Musa and those with him may cross, then close upon those of Pharaoh and his followers who remain behind." But Musa forgot to strike the sea with the staff, and he reached the sea with its roar, fearing that Musa might strike it with his staff while he was heedless, and thus become a disobedient one against Allah.

When the two hosts came into view of each other and drew near, the companions of Musa said, "Indeed, we are about to be overtaken." [Musa said], "Do what your Lord has commanded you, for He does not lie, nor has he lied." He said, "My Lord promised me that when I reached the sea it would split into twelve paths, until I crossed it." Then he remembered the staff after that, and struck the sea with his staff just as the vanguard of Pharaoh's army drew near the rear of Musa's army. The sea split as his Lord had commanded and as He had promised Musa. When Musa and all his companions had crossed the sea, and Pharaoh and his companions entered it, the sea closed over them as it had been commanded. When Musa crossed the sea, his companions said, "We fear that Pharaoh has not drowned, and we do not believe in his destruction." So he called upon his Lord, and He brought him out to them in his body, until they were certain of his destruction.

Then after that they passed by a people devoted to their idols. ﴿They said, "O Musa, make for us a god just as they have gods." He said, "Indeed you are a people who are ignorant. Indeed, these people — what they are engaged in is doomed, and what they have been doing is false"﴾ [Al-A'raf: 138-139]. "You have seen the lessons and heard what suffices you," and [Musa] went on. Musa settled them at a station and said [to them], "Obey Harun, for I have appointed him as your successor, and I am going to my Lord." He set for them a term of thirty days, in which he would return to them. When he came to his Lord and wished to speak with Him, [he had fasted] thirty days, its nights and days, and he disliked speaking with his Lord while his breath had the odor of a fasting person's mouth. So Musa took some of the plants of the earth and chewed it. When he came to Him, his Lord said to him, knowing well what had happened, "Why did you break your fast?" He said, "O my Lord, I disliked speaking to You except with a pleasant-smelling mouth." He said, "Do you not know, O Musa, that the breath of a fasting person's mouth is more fragrant than the scent of musk? Return, fast ten [more days], then come to Me." So Musa, peace be upon him, did what he was commanded. When the people of Musa saw that he had not returned to them within the term, it grieved them. Harun had addressed them, saying: "You have left Egypt, and the people of Pharaoh have with you loans and deposits, and you have similar things with them. I think you are reckoning what you have with them, but I do not permit you any deposit that was entrusted to you, nor any loan, and we shall neither return anything of that to them nor keep it for ourselves." He dug a pit and commanded every people who had any of those goods, whether property or jewelry, to throw it into that pit. Then he lit a fire upon it and burned it, and said, "It shall belong neither to us nor to them."

The Samiri was from a people who worshipped cattle, neighbors of the Children of Israel, but he was not one of the Children of Israel. He went along with Musa and the Children of Israel when they set out. It was decreed for him that he saw a trace [of the Messenger], so he took a handful of it. He passed by Harun, who said to him, "O Samiri, will you not throw what is in your hand?" And he was holding it, and no one could see it throughout that time. He said, "This is a handful from the trace of the Messenger who carried you across the sea. I will not throw it for anything, except that you ask Allah, when I throw it, that what I want may come to be." So he threw it, and Harun supplicated for him. He said, "I want it to be a calf." So what was in the pit of goods, jewelry, copper or iron came together, and it became a hollow calf with no spirit in it, but it had a lowing sound.

Ibn Abbas said: "No, by Allah, it never had any voice at all. Rather, the wind entered through its rear and exited through its mouth, and that sound was from that."

The Children of Israel then split into factions. One faction said, "O Samiri, what is this, when you know about it?" He said, "This is your Lord, but Musa has lost the way." Another faction said, "We will not deny this until Musa returns to us. If it is our Lord, we have not lost Him and we have not failed Him when we saw Him. But if it is not our Lord, then we will follow the word of Musa." Another faction said, "This is the work of Satan; it is not our Lord, and we do not believe in it or accept it." And a faction had the truth of what the Samiri said about the calf instilled in their hearts, and they openly denied [the Prophet]. Harun said to them: ﴿"O my people, you are only being tested by it, and indeed your Lord is the Most Merciful"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 90]. They said, "What is wrong with Musa?
