So enter upon them through the gate, and when you have entered it, you will surely be victorious." Some people say that they were from the people of Musa. But those who feared, the Children of Israel, said: ﴿O Musa, indeed we will never enter it as long as they are in it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight, indeed we are sitting here.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 24] So they angered Musa, and he prayed against them and called them corrupt (fasiqin), and he had not prayed against them before that, because of the disobedience he saw from them and their misconduct, until that day. Allah answered his prayer and called them corrupt just as he had called them so. He forbade it to them for forty years, wandering in the land; they would rise each morning and travel, having no place of rest. Then Allah shaded them with the cloud in the wilderness, sent down upon them the manna and the quails, made for them garments that would neither wear out nor become soiled, and placed among them a square stone. Musa was commanded to strike it with his staff, and twelve springs gushed forth from it, three springs in each direction, and Allah made known to each tribe its spring from which they would drink. They would not move from any stopping place without finding that stone with them, in the place where it had been the day before.

Ibn 'Abbas raised this narration to the Prophet (ﷺ), and what confirms it for me is that Mu'awiyah heard Ibn 'Abbas narrate this hadith, and he denied that the Pharaonic man was the one who disclosed to Musa the matter of the slain man whom he had killed. He said: "How could he have disclosed it when he had not known about it, and only the Israelite who was present at that had witnessed it?" Ibn 'Abbas became angry, took Mu'awiyah by the hand, went with him to Sa'd ibn Malik al-Zuhri, and said to him: "O Abu Ishaq, do you remember the day when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told us about the slain man of Musa who killed one of the family of Pharaoh? Was it the Israelite who disclosed the matter, or the Pharaonic man?" He said: "It was only the Pharaonic man who disclosed it, from what he heard from the Israelite who witnessed that and was present."

This was narrated by the Imam al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, and Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim both reported it in their tafsirs, all of them through the hadith of Yazid ibn Harun with the same chain. [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11326), and Tafsir al-Tabari (16/125).] It is a statement of Ibn 'Abbas himself (mawquf), and there is in it nothing raised (marfu') except a little of it. It seems that Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, took it from what is permitted to be transmitted from the Isra'iliyyat, from Ka'b al-Ahbar or others, and Allah knows best. I also heard our shaykh, the Hafiz Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, say the same.

This is an answer from Allah to His Messenger Musa, peace be upon him, regarding what he asked of his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, and a reminder to him of the past blessings He bestowed upon him, such as the inspiration He gave his mother while she was nursing him and was afraid for him from Pharaoh and his chiefs, that they would kill him. This was because he had been born in the year in which they were killing the boys. So she made him an ark (tabut), and she would nurse him, then place him in it and send it onto the river, which is the Nile, and she would hold it by a rope to her house. Once she went to tie it, but it slipped from her and the river carried it away. She was thereby struck with the grief and anguish that Allah mentioned about her in His saying: ﴿And the heart of the mother of Musa became empty. She was about to disclose him, had We not strengthened her heart so she would be of the believers﴾ [Al-Qasas: 10]. The river carried him to the house of Pharaoh, ﴿and the family of Pharaoh picked him up to be to them an enemy and a grief﴾ [Al-Qasas: 8], meaning a decree decreed by Allah, since they were the ones killing the boys of the Children of Israel out of fear of the existence of Musa. Allah, to whom belongs the great authority and complete power, decreed that he would be raised only on the bed of Pharaoh, and be nourished with his food and drink, along with Pharaoh's and his wife's love for him. Therefore He said: ﴿He will take him, My enemy and his enemy. And I bestowed upon you love from Me﴾ [meaning: among your enemy, I made him love you. Salamah ibn Kuhayl said regarding ﴿And I bestowed upon you love from Me﴾: "He said: I made you beloved to My servants."]

﴿And that you may be brought up under My eye﴾. Abu 'Imran al-Jawni said: "You would be raised under the eye of Allah."
Qatadah said: "You would be nourished under My eye."
Ma'mar ibn al-Muthanna said: "﴿And that you may be brought up under My eye﴾: in a manner where I see."
'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "That is, I would make him in the house of the king, enjoying blessings and luxury, his food with them being the food of the king. That is the making (sun'ah)."

* *

His saying: ﴿When your sister walked and said, "Shall I direct you to one who will be responsible for him?" So We returned you to your mother that her eye might be comforted and not grieve﴾. This is because, when he settled with the family of Pharaoh, they offered him wet nurses, but he refused them. Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And We had prohibited to him the wet nurses before﴾. So his sister came and said: ﴿Shall I direct you to a household who will raise him for you, and they will be sincere to him?﴾ [Al-Qasas: 12]. She meant: "Shall I direct you to one who will nurse him for you in exchange for a wage?" So she went with him, and they with her, to his mother, and she offered her breast to him, and he accepted it. They rejoiced greatly at that and hired her to nurse him. Thereby she gained happiness, elevation and comfort in this world and in the Hereafter, which is more abundant and more generous. Therefore it has come in a hadith: "The example of the craftsman who seeks reward in his craft for good is like the mother of Musa, who nurses her child and takes her wage." [Abu Dawud related it in al-Marasil, no. 332, through the route of Jubayr ibn Nufayr, similarly, and its wording is: "The example of those among my nation who fight and take the reward, and strengthen themselves against their enemy by it, is like the mother of Musa, who nurses her child and takes her wage."]

And the Most High said here: ﴿So We returned you to your mother that her eye might be comforted and not grieve﴾, meaning: over you. ﴿And you killed a soul﴾, meaning the Copt. ﴿And We delivered you from distress﴾, which is what befell him because of the determination of the family of Pharaoh to kill him, so he fled from them, running away, until he reached the water of Madyan. And that righteous man said to him: ﴿Fear not. You have escaped from the wrongdoing people﴾ [Al-Qasas: 25].

* *

His saying: ﴿And We tried you with a [severe] trial﴾. Imam Abu 'Abd al-Rahman Ahmad ibn Shu'ayb al-Nasa'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said in the Book of Tafsir in his Sunan, regarding His saying: ﴿And We tried you with a [severe] trial﴾: The hadith of the trials (al-futun):

Abdullah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Asbagh ibn Zayd informed us, al-Qasim ibn Abi Ayyub narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Jubayr informed me, who said: I asked Abdullah ibn 'Abbas about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to Musa, peace be upon him: ﴿And We tried you with a [severe] trial﴾, and I asked him what al-futun is. He said: "Resume the day, O son of Jubayr, for it has a long story." When I woke in the morning, I went to Ibn 'Abbas to fulfil from him what he had promised me of the hadith of the trials. He said: "Pharaoh and his companions discussed what Allah had promised Ibrahim, peace be upon him, that He would place in his descendants prophets and kings. Some of them said: 'The Children of Israel are awaiting that, and they have no doubt about it, and they thought it was Yusuf ibn Ya'qub.' When he died they said: 'That was not the promise of Ibrahim.' Pharaoh said: 'So how do you see it?' They conferred and agreed on a plan to send men with them carrying knives, going around among the Children of Israel, so that they would not find any male newborn without slaughtering him. They did so. When they saw that the elders of the Children of Israel were dying by their appointed times while the young were being slaughtered, they said: 'Soon you will destroy the Children of Israel, and you will come to be engaged in the work and service that they used to perform for you. So kill every male newborn in one year, and leave a year without killing any of them, so that the young will grow to replace those of the elders who die. For they will not increase in number by those you spare and fear their outnumbering you, nor will they be destroyed by those you kill and need them.' So they agreed on that."

Umm Musa conceived Harun in the year in which the boys were not slaughtered, and she gave birth to him openly and safely. When the following year came, she conceived Musa, peace be upon him, and anxiety and sorrow fell into her heart. That was of the trials, O son of Jubayr, that entered upon him in his mother's womb, of what was intended for him. Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, inspired to her that ﴿Do not fear and do not grieve. Indeed, We will return him to you and make him one of the messengers﴾ [Al-Qasas: 7]. He commanded her, when she gave birth, to place him in an ark and then throw him into the river (al-yamm). When she gave birth she did so, and when her son disappeared from her, Satan came to her and she said to herself: "What has become of my son? If he had been slaughtered before me, I would have buried him and shrouded him, and that would be more beloved to me than throwing him to the creatures and fish of the sea."

The water carried him until it brought him to the landing place of the water-drawing of Pharaoh's wife's maidservants. When they saw him, they took him and wanted to open the ark. Some of them said: "In this is wealth. If we open it, the queen will not believe us about what we found in it." So they carried it as it was, without taking anything out of it, until they lifted it to her. When she opened it she saw a boy, and there was cast upon him from her a love such as had never been cast upon anyone else. The heart of Umm Musa became empty of the remembrance of everything except the remembrance of Musa.

When the slaughterers heard of his matter, they came with their knives to the wife of Pharaoh to slaughter him. That was from the trials, O son of Jubayr. She said to them: "Leave him, for this one will not increase the Children of Israel. Until I go to Pharaoh and ask him to grant him to me. If he grants him to me, you will have done well and fairly, and if he orders his slaughter, I will not blame you."

She went to Pharaoh and said: ﴿The comfort of the eye for me and for you﴾ [Al-Qasas: 9]. Pharaoh said: "He will be yours, but as for me, I have no need of him." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, if Pharaoh had agreed that he would be a comfort of the eye for him as his wife did, Allah would have guided him as He guided her, but Allah deprived him of that." She sent to those around her, to every woman who had milk, to choose a wet nurse for him. Whenever a woman took him to nurse him, he would not turn to her breast, until the wife of Pharaoh feared that he would refuse milk and die. That saddened her, so she ordered him to be taken out to the market and the gathering of people, hoping to find a wet nurse from whom he would take. But he did not accept. Umm Musa became distraught, and she said to his sister: "Follow his trail and search for him, and see if you hear any mention of him, is my son alive or have the beasts eaten him?" She forgot what Allah had promised her. His sister saw him from afar while they did not notice, (al-junub: that a person's sight reaches a distant thing while it is beside him and he does not notice it). She said, out of joy, when the nurses had exhausted them: "I will direct you to a household who will raise him for you, and they will be sincere to him." They took her and said: "How do you know? What is their sincerity to him? Do they know him?" until they doubted in that, and that was from the trials, O son of Jubayr. She said: "Their sincerity to him and their compassion for him is their desire for the king's nursing and their hope for the king's benefit." They sent her, and she went to her mother and informed her of the news. His mother came, and when she placed him in her lap, he lunged at her breast and sucked it until his sides were filled with satisfaction. The messengers went to the wife of Pharaoh, giving her good news that we have found a wet nurse for your son. She sent for her. They brought her and him, and when she saw how he behaved with her, she said: "Stay and nurse my son, for I have never loved anything as I love him." Umm Musa said: "I cannot leave my house and my child to be lost. If you are content to give him to me, I will take him to my house, and he will be with me, and I will not neglect him in goodness [if you do, and if not], for I will not leave my house and my child." Umm Musa remembered what Allah had promised her, so she refused the wife of Pharaoh, and she was certain that Allah would fulfil His promise. She returned with him to her house that same day, and Allah made him grow well and preserved him for what He had decreed concerning him.

The Children of Israel remained in the outskirts of the town, refusing forced labour and oppression as much as they could. When Musa grew up, Pharaoh's wife said to Musa's mother: "Will you let me see my son?" So she promised her a day on which she would show him to her. Pharaoh's wife also said to her treasurers, her wet-nurses and her stewards: "None of you should fail to meet my son today with a gift and an honour, so that I may see that. And I am sending a trustworthy agent to count what each of you does." The gifts, the gratuities and the honours continued to greet him from the moment he left his mother's house until he entered Pharaoh's wife's presence. When he entered upon her, she gave him gifts, honoured him and rejoiced in him, and she rewarded his mother for the good care she had given him. Then she said: "I will bring him to Pharaoh so that he may give him gifts and honour him." When she brought him in to Pharaoh, Pharaoh placed him in his lap. Musa took hold of Pharaoh's beard and pulled it down towards the ground. The deluded enemies of Allah said to Pharaoh: "Do you not see what Allah promised Ibrahim, His prophet? He claimed that he would inherit you, overcome you and throw you down." So Pharaoh sent for the slaughterers to kill him. This was one of the trials, O Ibn Jubayr, after every affliction with which he was tested, and it was intended for him as a trial.

Then Pharaoh's wife came and said: "What has become of you regarding this boy whom you gave to me?" Pharaoh said: "Do you not see that he claims he will throw me down and overcome me?" She said: "Set between me and you a matter by which the truth will be known. Bring two embers and two pearls, and bring them near to him. If he reaches for the pearls and avoids the embers, then you will know that he understands. But if he takes the embers and does not want the pearls, you will know that no one who understands would prefer the embers over the pearls." So they brought them near to him, and he took the embers. Pharaoh snatched them from him, fearing that they would burn his hand. Pharaoh's wife said: "Do you not see?" Then Allah turned him away from them after he had intended to harm him, and Allah accomplishes His command.

When he reached his maturity and became a man, none of Pharaoh's household could approach any of the Children of Israel with oppression or forced labour while he was with them, until they withdrew entirely. One day, while Musa, peace be upon him, was walking in the outskirts of the city, he came upon two men fighting, one of them from Pharaoh's people and the other from the Children of Israel. The Israelite called on him for help against the Egyptian, so Musa became exceedingly angry, because he had struck him while knowing his standing among the Children of Israel and his protection of them. People did not know anything except that this was from the nursing, except Musa's mother, unless Allah (Subhanahu) had informed Musa of something about it that He had not informed anyone else. So Musa struck the Egyptian and killed him, and no one saw the two of them except Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the Israelite. When Musa killed the man, he said: ﴿This is from the work of Satan. Indeed, he is a clear, misleading enemy﴾ [al-Qasas: 15]. Then he said: ﴿My Lord, indeed I have wronged myself, so forgive me.﴾ So He forgave him. Indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful [al-Qasas: 16]. He woke in the city fearful, awaiting news. Then he went to Pharaoh, and it was said to him: "The Children of Israel have killed a man from the household of Pharaoh, so take our right and do not show them leniency." Pharaoh said: "Find me his killer and whoever will testify against him, for the king, even if he inclines towards his own people, cannot properly exact retribution without evidence and proof. So seek out for me the knowledge of this, and I will take your right for you." While they were searching and could not find any proof, behold, on the following day Musa saw that Israelite fighting another man from Pharaoh's household. The Israelite called on him for help against the Egyptian. Musa encountered him, regretting what he had done and disliking what he had seen. The Israelite became angry, wanting to strike the Egyptian. So Musa said to the Israelite, because of what he had done yesterday and today: ﴿Indeed, you are a clear transgressor﴾. The Israelite looked at Musa after he had said what he said, and saw that he was angry, just as he had been angry the day before when he killed the Egyptian. He feared that, after he had said to him, ﴿Indeed, you are a clear transgressor﴾ [al-Qasas: 18], Musa intended to strike him, when in fact he did not intend that but intended the Egyptian. The Israelite became afraid and said: ﴿O Musa, do you intend to kill me as you killed a soul yesterday?﴾ [al-Qasas: 19]. He said this only out of fear that Musa intended to kill him. So they parted, and the Egyptian went and informed them of what he had heard from the Israelite of the report when he said: ﴿Do you intend to kill me as you killed a soul yesterday?﴾ Then Pharaoh sent the slaughterers to kill Musa. But Musa took the main road, walking calmly, seeking Musa, while they did not fear that he would escape them. Then a man from the followers of Musa came from the farthest part of the city, took a shortcut and got ahead of them to Musa, and informed him of the news. This too was a trial, O Ibn Jubayr.

So Musa left, heading towards Madyan. He had not encountered any affliction before that, and he had no knowledge of the way except his good opinion of his Lord, Mighty and Majestic. He said: ﴿Perhaps my Lord will guide me to the right way﴾. When he arrived at the water of Madyan, he found a community of people watering their flocks, and besides them he found two women holding back [their flocks] [al-Qasas: 22–23].

That is, the two women were holding back their sheep. He said to them: "What is your business? Why do you stay apart and not water with the people?" They said: "We have no strength to compete with the people; we only wait for what is left over of their watering troughs." So he watered for them, drawing a great deal of water in the bucket until he was the first of the shepherds. The two women returned to their father with their sheep, and Musa, peace be upon him, withdrew and sat in the shade of a tree, and said: ﴿My Lord, indeed I am in need of whatever good You send down to me﴾ [al-Qasas: 24]. Their father was surprised at how quickly they returned with their sheep, full-uddered and well-fed, and he said: "You have something unusual today." They informed him of what Musa had done. So he commanded one of them to call him, and she went to Musa and called him. When he spoke with him, he said: ﴿Do not fear; you have escaped from the wrongdoing people﴾ [al-Qasas: 25]. Pharaoh and his people have no authority over us, and we are not in his kingdom. One of the two women said: ﴿O my father, hire him; indeed the best one you can hire is the strong and trustworthy﴾ [al-Qasas: 26]. Jealousy overcame him so that he said to her: "What do you know of his strength? And of his trustworthiness?" She said: "As for his strength, I saw from him, in the bucket when he watered for us, that I had never seen a man stronger in that watering than him. As for his trustworthiness, he looked at me when I approached him and walked towards him. When he knew that I was a woman, he lowered his head and did not raise it until I had conveyed your message to him. Then he said to me: 'Walk behind me and direct me to the way.' He would not have done this unless he was trustworthy." So her father was relieved and believed her, and he thought well of him what she had said.

He said to him: ﴿Would you like me to marry you to one of these two daughters of mine on condition that you serve me for eight years? And if you complete ten, then it is from you. I do not want to burden you. You will find me, if Allah wills, among the righteous﴾ [al-Qasas: 27]. He agreed, so it was incumbent upon the prophet of Allah, Musa, to serve for eight years, and two years were a favour from him. Allah fulfilled his obligation on his behalf, and so he completed ten.

Sa'id (that is, Ibn Jubayr) said: A man from among the Christians, one of their scholars, met me and said: "Do you know which of the two terms Musa fulfilled?" I said: "No," and at that time I did not know. Then I met Ibn 'Abbas and mentioned this to him. He said: "Do you not know that eight years were obligatory upon the prophet of Allah? It was not for the prophet of Allah to reduce any of it, and he knew that Allah would fulfil on Musa's behalf the term He had promised him, so he fulfilled ten years." Then I met the Christian and informed him of that. He said: "The one you asked, who informed you, knows better than you about that." I said: "Indeed, and more deserving [of knowing it]."

When Musa travelled with his family, there occurred the matter of the fire, the staff and his hand, which Allah related to you in the Qur'an. He complained to Allah, exalted is He, about what he feared from the household of Pharaoh regarding the man he had killed, and about the knot in his tongue, for there was a knot in his tongue that prevented him from much speech. He asked his Lord to help him through his brother Harun, to be a supporter for him and to speak on his behalf about much that his tongue could not express clearly. Allah granted him his request, loosened the knot in his tongue, and revealed to Harun, commanding him to meet him. So Musa set off with his staff until he met Harun, peace be upon them both. Then they both set out to Pharaoh and stood at his door for a while without being admitted. Then he admitted them after a severe barrier, and they said: ﴿Indeed, we are two messengers of your Lord﴾ [Ta-Ha: 47]. He said: "Who is your Lord?" They informed him of what Allah related to you in the Qur'an. He said: "What do you want?" They reminded him of the slain man, and he excused himself with what you have heard. He said: "I want you to believe in Allah and to send the Children of Israel with me." He refused him and said: ﴿So bring a sign, if you are among the truthful﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 154]. Then he threw his staff, and behold, it became a huge, swiftly moving serpent with its mouth wide open, rushing towards Pharaoh. When Pharaoh saw it approaching him, he feared it, leapt from his throne and called upon Musa to hold it back from him. Musa did so. Then he took his hand out of his garment, and it appeared white without any defect, meaning without leprosy. Then he returned it, and it went back to its former colour. Pharaoh consulted the chiefs around him about what he had seen. They said to him: ﴿These two are sorcerers who want to drive you out of your land with their sorcery and do away with your most exemplary way of life﴾ [Ta-Ha: 63], meaning their kingdom in which they were living, and their livelihood. They refused to give Musa anything of what he requested, and they said to him: "Gather the sorcerers, for they are many in your land, so that you may overcome their sorcery with your sorcery." So he sent to the cities, and every sorcerer who was learned in magic was gathered for him. When they came to Pharaoh, they said: "What does this sorcerer do?" They said: "He works with serpents." They said: "By Allah, no one on earth works with sorcery of serpents, ropes and staves as we do. What will be our reward if we overcome him?" He said to them: "You are my relatives and my close associates, and I will do for you everything you desire." So they agreed upon the day of the adornment, and that the people should be gathered in the forenoon.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Ibn 'Abbas told me that the day of the adornment on which Allah made Musa prevail over Pharaoh and the sorcerers was the day of 'Ashura (the tenth of Muharram).

When they gathered at one place, the people said to one another: "Come, let us attend this affair, ﴿so that we may follow the sorcerers, if they are the victors﴾" [Ash-Shu'ara: 40]. They meant Musa and Harun, mocking them. Then they said, "O Musa, ﴿either you throw, or we will be the ones who throw﴾" [Al-A'raf: 115], trusting in their own power through their sorcery. ﴿He said, "Rather, you throw"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 66]. ﴿So they threw their ropes and their staffs, and said, "By the might of Pharaoh, we are indeed the victors"﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 44]. Musa saw from their sorcery what made him feel fear within himself. So Allah revealed to him, "Throw your staff." When he threw it, it became a great serpent, its mouth wide open. The staffs began to entwine with the ropes until they became food for the serpent, entering into it, until it left no staff or rope [in one version: "rope"] unswallowed. When the sorcerers realized this, they said, "If this were sorcery, it would not have reached this extent of our sorcery. Rather, it is a command from Allah, Mighty and Majestic. We believe in Allah and in what Musa has brought, and we repent to Allah of what we were upon." So Allah broke the back of Pharaoh in that place, and [broke] his followers, and the truth became manifest, and what they had been doing was nullified. ﴿So they were defeated there and returned in humiliation﴾ [Al-A'raf: 119]. Pharaoh's wife was openly present, in humble attire, calling upon Allah for victory for Musa over Pharaoh and his followers. Whoever among Pharaoh's family saw her thought that she had only humbled herself out of compassion for Pharaoh and his followers, but her grief and concern were for Musa.

When Musa's stay was prolonged with Pharaoh's false promises, every time he brought a sign, Pharaoh promised him at that point that he would send the Children of Israel with him. But once it passed, he broke his promise and said, "Can your Lord produce anything other than this?" So Allah sent upon his people the flood, the locusts, the lice, the frogs and the blood as distinct signs. Each time, [Pharaoh] complained to Musa and asked him to remove it from him, and he made a covenant with him that he would send the Children of Israel with him. But once it was removed, he broke his promise and violated his covenant.

Until Allah commanded Musa to depart with his people, so he set out with them at night. When Pharaoh awoke in the morning and saw that they had gone, he sent [messengers] to the cities to gather [people], and he pursued them with a great and numerous army. Allah revealed to the sea: "When My servant Musa strikes you with his staff, split into twelve paths, so that Musa and those with him may cross, then close upon those of Pharaoh and his followers who remain behind." But Musa forgot to strike the sea with the staff, and he reached the sea with its roar, fearing that Musa might strike it with his staff while he was heedless, and thus become a disobedient one against Allah.

When the two hosts came into view of each other and drew near, the companions of Musa said, "Indeed, we are about to be overtaken." [Musa said], "Do what your Lord has commanded you, for He does not lie, nor has he lied." He said, "My Lord promised me that when I reached the sea it would split into twelve paths, until I crossed it." Then he remembered the staff after that, and struck the sea with his staff just as the vanguard of Pharaoh's army drew near the rear of Musa's army. The sea split as his Lord had commanded and as He had promised Musa. When Musa and all his companions had crossed the sea, and Pharaoh and his companions entered it, the sea closed over them as it had been commanded. When Musa crossed the sea, his companions said, "We fear that Pharaoh has not drowned, and we do not believe in his destruction." So he called upon his Lord, and He brought him out to them in his body, until they were certain of his destruction.

Then after that they passed by a people devoted to their idols. ﴿They said, "O Musa, make for us a god just as they have gods." He said, "Indeed you are a people who are ignorant. Indeed, these people — what they are engaged in is doomed, and what they have been doing is false"﴾ [Al-A'raf: 138-139]. "You have seen the lessons and heard what suffices you," and [Musa] went on. Musa settled them at a station and said [to them], "Obey Harun, for I have appointed him as your successor, and I am going to my Lord." He set for them a term of thirty days, in which he would return to them. When he came to his Lord and wished to speak with Him, [he had fasted] thirty days, its nights and days, and he disliked speaking with his Lord while his breath had the odor of a fasting person's mouth. So Musa took some of the plants of the earth and chewed it. When he came to Him, his Lord said to him, knowing well what had happened, "Why did you break your fast?" He said, "O my Lord, I disliked speaking to You except with a pleasant-smelling mouth." He said, "Do you not know, O Musa, that the breath of a fasting person's mouth is more fragrant than the scent of musk? Return, fast ten [more days], then come to Me." So Musa, peace be upon him, did what he was commanded. When the people of Musa saw that he had not returned to them within the term, it grieved them. Harun had addressed them, saying: "You have left Egypt, and the people of Pharaoh have with you loans and deposits, and you have similar things with them. I think you are reckoning what you have with them, but I do not permit you any deposit that was entrusted to you, nor any loan, and we shall neither return anything of that to them nor keep it for ourselves." He dug a pit and commanded every people who had any of those goods, whether property or jewelry, to throw it into that pit. Then he lit a fire upon it and burned it, and said, "It shall belong neither to us nor to them."

The Samiri was from a people who worshipped cattle, neighbors of the Children of Israel, but he was not one of the Children of Israel. He went along with Musa and the Children of Israel when they set out. It was decreed for him that he saw a trace [of the Messenger], so he took a handful of it. He passed by Harun, who said to him, "O Samiri, will you not throw what is in your hand?" And he was holding it, and no one could see it throughout that time. He said, "This is a handful from the trace of the Messenger who carried you across the sea. I will not throw it for anything, except that you ask Allah, when I throw it, that what I want may come to be." So he threw it, and Harun supplicated for him. He said, "I want it to be a calf." So what was in the pit of goods, jewelry, copper or iron came together, and it became a hollow calf with no spirit in it, but it had a lowing sound.

Ibn Abbas said: "No, by Allah, it never had any voice at all. Rather, the wind entered through its rear and exited through its mouth, and that sound was from that."

The Children of Israel then split into factions. One faction said, "O Samiri, what is this, when you know about it?" He said, "This is your Lord, but Musa has lost the way." Another faction said, "We will not deny this until Musa returns to us. If it is our Lord, we have not lost Him and we have not failed Him when we saw Him. But if it is not our Lord, then we will follow the word of Musa." Another faction said, "This is the work of Satan; it is not our Lord, and we do not believe in it or accept it." And a faction had the truth of what the Samiri said about the calf instilled in their hearts, and they openly denied [the Prophet]. Harun said to them: ﴿"O my people, you are only being tested by it, and indeed your Lord is the Most Merciful"﴾ [Ta-Ha: 90]. They said, "What is wrong with Musa? He promised us thirty days, then broke his promise to us; these are forty days that have passed." Their foolish ones said, "He has erred from his Lord, and he is seeking Him and following Him."

When Allah spoke to Musa and said to him what He said, He informed him of what his people had encountered after him. ﴿So Musa returned to his people, angry and grieved﴾ [Ta-Ha: 86]. He said to them what you have heard in the Qur'an, and he took his brother by the head, dragging him toward himself, and threw down the Tablets in anger. Then he excused his brother with his excuse, sought forgiveness for him, and turned to the Samiri and said to him, "What led you to do what you did?" He said, "I took a handful from the trace of the Messenger, and I understood it, but it was hidden from you, so I threw it." ﴿"Thus my soul prompted me." He said, "Then go, for it is yours in this life to say, 'No touching,' and indeed you have an appointment that you will not be able to break. Look at your god to which you have remained devoted; we will surely burn it, then scatter it into the sea in scattered fragments."﴾ [Ta-Ha: 96-97]. And if it had been a god, it would not have been able to escape that from him. So the Children of Israel were certain of the trial, and those whose opinion was like the opinion of Harun were pleased, and they said to their community, "O Musa, ask your Lord to open for us a door of repentance that we may perform, so that He may expiate for us what we have done." So Musa chose seventy men from his people for that, the best of the Children of Israel, and those who had not associated with the calf. He set out with them, asking for repentance on their behalf. Then the earth shook beneath them, and the prophet of Allah felt shame before his people and his delegation, when what was done to them was done. He said: ﴿"My Lord, had You willed, You would have destroyed them before, and me as well. Will You destroy us for what the foolish among us have done?"﴾ [Al-A'raf: 155]. Among them were those whom Allah had discerned to have had the love of the calf instilled in their hearts and belief in it, and for that the earth shook beneath them. He said: ﴿"My mercy encompasses all things, and I will prescribe it for those who fear Allah, pay the zakat, and those who believe in Our signs, who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet, whom they find written with them in the Torah and the Gospel"﴾ [Al-A'raf: 156-157]. Musa said, "My Lord, I asked You for repentance for my people, and You said, 'Indeed I have prescribed My mercy for a people other than your people.' Why did You not delay me until You bring me forth in the community of that merciful man?" He said to him: "Indeed, their repentance is that each man among them kill whoever he meets of his father or his son, killing him with the sword, and let him not mind whom he kills in that place." Those who had been hidden from Musa and Harun repented, and Allah had discerned their sins, so they confessed them and did what they were commanded. Allah forgave both the killer and the killed.

Then Musa (peace be upon him) set out with them, heading toward the Holy Land, and he took up the Tablets after the anger had subsided from him. He commanded them to do what he had been commanded to convey to them of the duties, but this was burdensome for them, and they refused to acknowledge them. So Allah lifted the mountain over them as though it were a canopy, and it drew near to them until they feared it would fall upon them. They took the Book with their right hands while they were looking at the mountain, with the Book in their hands, and they were behind the mountain, fearing that it would fall upon them. Then they went on until they reached the Holy Land, and they found a city in which there were a people of tyrants whose physique was of an unusual form, and they mentioned some marvellous things about the size of their fruits. They said: "O Musa, indeed there are in it a people of tyrants, and we have no power to face them, and we will not enter it as long as they are in it. But if they leave it, then we will enter." Two men from among those who feared (it was said to Yazid: "Did he recite it thus?" He said: "Yes, 'from among the tyrants'") said, having believed in Musa and gone out to him: "We know better about our people. If you are only afraid of what you have seen of their bodies and their numbers, then indeed they have no hearts and no strength among them. So enter upon them through the gate, and when you have entered it, you will surely be victorious." Some people say that they were from the people of Musa. But those who feared, the Children of Israel, said: ﴿O Musa, indeed we will never enter it as long as they are in it. So go, you and your Lord, and fight, indeed we are sitting here.﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 24] So they angered Musa, and he prayed against them and called them corrupt (fasiqin), and he had not prayed against them before that, because of the disobedience he saw from them and their misconduct, until that day. Allah answered his prayer and called them corrupt just as he had called them so. He forbade it to them for forty years, wandering in the land; they would rise each morning and travel, having no place of rest. Then Allah shaded them with the cloud in the wilderness, sent down upon them the manna and the quails, made for them garments that would neither wear out nor become soiled, and placed among them a square stone. Musa was commanded to strike it with his staff, and twelve springs gushed forth from it, three springs in each direction, and Allah made known to each tribe its spring from which they would drink. They would not move from any stopping place without finding that stone with them, in the place where it had been the day before.

Ibn 'Abbas raised this narration to the Prophet (ﷺ), and what confirms it for me is that Mu'awiyah heard Ibn 'Abbas narrate this hadith, and he denied that the Pharaonic man was the one who disclosed to Musa the matter of the slain man whom he had killed. He said: "How could he have disclosed it when he had not known about it, and only the Israelite who was present at that had witnessed it?" Ibn 'Abbas became angry, took Mu'awiyah by the hand, went with him to Sa'd ibn Malik al-Zuhri, and said to him: "O Abu Ishaq, do you remember the day when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) told us about the slain man of Musa who killed one of the family of Pharaoh? Was it the Israelite who disclosed the matter, or the Pharaonic man?" He said: "It was only the Pharaonic man who disclosed it, from what he heard from the Israelite who witnessed that and was present."

This was narrated by the Imam al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, and Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim both reported it in their tafsirs, all of them through the hadith of Yazid ibn Harun with the same chain. [Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11326), and Tafsir al-Tabari (16/125).] It is a statement of Ibn 'Abbas himself (mawquf), and there is in it nothing raised (marfu') except a little of it. It seems that Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, took it from what is permitted to be transmitted from the Isra'iliyyat, from Ka'b al-Ahbar or others, and Allah knows best. I also heard our shaykh, the Hafiz Abu al-Hajjaj al-Mizzi, say the same.

Ibn Kathir said, addressing Musa (peace be upon him): He remained as a resident among the people of Madyan (Midian), fleeing from Fir'awn (Pharaoh) and his chiefs, tending sheep in return for his father-in-law's service, until the term was completed and the appointed time had passed. Then he came, in accordance with the decree and will of Allah and without a prior appointment. The whole affair belongs to Allah [[In MS. F: "له" (to Him).]], blessed and exalted, who directs His servants and creation as He wills. For this reason He said: ﴿Then you came at an appointed time, O Musa﴾ [[Added from MS. F and MS. A.]]. Mujahid said: that is, at a set time.

It is reported from Ikrimah concerning His words ﴿speak to him with gentle speech﴾ that he said: "There is no god but Allah." Amr ibn Ubayd narrated from al-Hasan al-Basri: ﴿speak to him with gentle speech﴾ means: "Give him an excuse. Say to him: 'Indeed you have a Lord, and you have a return, and before you is a Garden and a Fire.'"

Baqiyyah narrated from Ali ibn Harun, from a man, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim, from al-Nazzal ibn Sabrah, from Ali: concerning His words ﴿speak to him with gentle speech﴾ he said: "Address him by his kunyah" [[Kunyah: a teknonym, a name formed from "Abu" plus a son's name.]].

It is similarly narrated from Sufyan al-Thawri: "Address him as Abu Murrah."

The conclusion from their statements is that their call to him should be made with soft, gentle, close and easy speech, so that it will have a greater effect on souls, be more eloquent and more effective, as Allah said: ﴿Invite to the way of your Lord with wisdom and good instruction, and argue with them in the best manner﴾ [al-Nahl: 125].

His words ﴿perhaps he will be reminded or fear﴾ mean: perhaps he will turn back from what he is in of misguidance and ruin. ﴿Or fear﴾ means: he will develop obedience out of fear of his Lord, as Allah said: [[The quotation that follows, ﴿for whoever wishes to be mindful or to fear﴾, is not a verse, as stated in all copies.]] ﴿For whoever wishes to remember or to fear﴾. So "remembering" means turning back from what is feared, and "fear" means attaining obedience.

Al-Hasan al-Basri, [regarding His words] [[Added from MS. A.]] ﴿perhaps he will be reminded or fear﴾, said: "Do not say, you O Musa and your brother Harun: 'Destroy him before I give him an excuse.'" [[In MS. F: "تعذرا"; in MS. A: "يعذر".]]

Here we mention the poem of Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl, which is also narrated for Umayyah ibn Abi al-Salt, as recorded by Ibn Ishaq:

*You are the one who, by grace and mercy,*
*sent to Musa a messenger calling out...*

*You said to him: "Go, and let Harun call with him*
*to Allah against Fir'awn, who was a transgressor..."*

*Tell him: "Did you set this [sky] level*
*without pillars, until it stood firm as it is?"*

*Tell him: "Did you raise this [sky] without supports?
May you be more gentle as its builder..."*

*Tell him: "Did you set its middle,*
*a light, when the night covers it, as a guide?"*

*Tell him: "Who brings out the sun in the morning,*
*so that it shines upon whatever the earth touches?"*

*Tell him: "Who causes the grain to sprout in the soil,*
*so that from it the herbage rises, swaying high?"*

*And who brings forth from it its grain in its heads;
in that are signs for whoever has understanding* [[In MS. A: "دويبة" (creature).]] [[Ibn Hisham's al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah, 1/228.]].

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said, relating what Allah says about Musa and Harun, peace be upon them both, that they said, seeking refuge in Allah and complaining to Him: ﴿Our Lord, we fear that he will hasten against us or that he will transgress.﴾ They meant that he might quickly inflict punishment on them, or that he might overstep against them and punish them when they do not deserve that from him.

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd said: ﴿an yafruṭa﴾ means "to hasten" (yaʿjala).

Mujahid said: "yabsuṭa ʿalayna" (he might stretch out against us).

al-Dahhak, from Ibn ʿAbbas, said: ﴿aw an yaṭghā﴾ means "yaʿtadiya" (he might transgress).

﴿He said: "Do not fear. Indeed, I am with you both; I hear and I see."﴾ That is: do not fear him, for indeed I am with you both. I hear your speech and his speech, and I see your place and his place. Nothing of your affair is hidden from Me. Know that his forelock is in My hand; he does not speak, breathe, or strike except with My permission and after My command. I am with you both through My protection, My help, and My support.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Our father related to us, ʿAli ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi related to us, Abu Muʿawiya related to us, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿAmr ibn Murrah, from Abu ʿUbayda, from ʿAbd Allah (Ibn Masʿud), who said: When Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent Musa to Pharaoh, he said: "My Lord, what should I say?" He said: "Say: Hayya Sharahayya." Al-Aʿmash said: its explanation is: "The Living before everything, and the Living after everything."

Its chain is good, but the report is strange (gharib).

﴿So go to him and say: "Indeed we are two messengers of your Lord."﴾ It has already been mentioned in the hadith of "al-Futun" from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: "They both stayed at his door for a while, not being admitted, and then he admitted them after a severe chamberlain-screening."

Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar mentioned that Musa and his brother Harun went out and stood at Pharaoh's door, seeking permission to see him, saying: "We are messengers of the Lord of the worlds. Announce us to this man." So they stayed, as I have been told, for two years, going and coming, while he did not know of them, and no one dared to inform him of their affair, until a jester of his entered upon him to amuse him and make him laugh. He said to him: "O King, at your door there is a man saying a strange saying; he claims that he has a god other than you, who sent him to you." He said: "At my door?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Bring him in." So he entered with his brother Harun, and in his hand was his staff. When he stood before Pharaoh, he said: "I am a messenger of the Lord of the worlds." Pharaoh recognized him.

al-Suddi mentioned that when he came to the land of Egypt, he was a guest of his mother and brother, and they did not recognize him. Their food that night was al-tatha'lil, which is al-lift (radish). Then they recognized him and greeted him. Musa said to him: "O Harun, my Lord has commanded me to go to this man Pharaoh and call him to Allah, and He commanded that you assist me." He said: "Do what your Lord has commanded you." So they went, and that was at night. Musa struck the palace door with his staff, and Pharaoh heard it and became angry and said: "Who dares to do this deed?" The attendants and doorkeepers informed him that there was a madman here claiming to be a messenger of Allah. He said: "Bring him to me." When they stood before him, they spoke, and he said to them what Allah mentioned in His Book.

* *

His saying: ﴿We have come to you with a sign from your Lord﴾ means: with a proof and a miracle from your Lord. ﴿And peace is upon those who follow guidance﴾ means: and peace be upon you if you follow guidance.

For this reason, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wrote to Heraclius, the great of the Romans, a letter beginning: "In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. From Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, to Heraclius, the great of the Romans: Peace be upon those who follow guidance. To proceed: I invite you with the call of Islam. Embrace Islam and you will be safe, and Allah will give you your reward twice."

Likewise, when Musaylima wrote to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a letter whose form was: "From Musaylima, the Messenger of Allah, to Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah: Peace be upon you. To proceed: I have been made a partner with you in the matter, so for you is the town and for me is the wilderness, but Quraysh are a people who transgress." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wrote back to him: "From Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, to Musaylima the Liar: Peace be upon those who follow guidance. To proceed: Indeed the earth belongs to Allah; He gives it as an inheritance to whomever He wills of His servants, and the final outcome is for the righteous." (Al-Sira al-Nabawiyya of Ibn Hisham, 2/600.)

﴿Then who is your Lord, O Musa?﴾ That is, who is the one who sent you and dispatched you? Indeed, I do not know Him, and I do not know any god for you other than me.

﴿Our Lord is He who gave everything its creation, then guided it.﴾

ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭalḥah related from Ibn ʿAbbās that he said: He created a mate for everything.

al-Ḍaḥḥāk related from Ibn ʿAbbās: He made the human a human, the donkey a donkey, and the sheep a sheep.

Layth ibn Abī Sulaym related from Mujāhid: He gave everything its form.

Ibn Abī Najīḥ related from Mujāhid: He perfected the creation of every living creature.

Saʿīd ibn Jubayr said regarding His saying, ﴿gave everything its creation, then guided it﴾: He gave every creature what would make it fit from its own kind. He did not make the human's kind that of the animal, nor the animal's kind that of the dog, nor the dog's kind that of the sheep. He gave every thing what is fitting for it in marriage, and He prepared every thing for that. None of them resembles any of His actions in creation, provision, or marriage.

Some of the exegetes said: ﴿gave everything its creation, then guided it﴾ is like His saying: ﴿And who determined and then guided﴾ (Al-Aʿlā: 3). He, may He be exalted, reports about the magicians when they came to an agreement with Moses, peace be upon him, that they said to Moses: ﴿Either you throw﴾, meaning you first, ﴿either you throw, or we will be the first to throw.﴾ He said, ﴿Rather, you throw.﴾ meaning you first, so that they might see what they would do of magic, and so that their affair would become clear to the people. ﴿Suddenly their ropes and their staffs, by their magic, seemed to him to be moving.﴾ In another verse, when they had thrown, ﴿they said, "By the might of Pharaoh, we are surely the victors."﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 44]. He, may He be exalted, also said: ﴿They bewitched the eyes of the people and terrified them, and they produced a great magic.﴾ [Al-A'raf: 116]. And here He said: ﴿Suddenly their ropes and their staffs, by their magic, seemed to him to be moving.﴾

That was because they had put into them enough mercury that they moved, shook and swayed because of it, so that it seemed to the onlooker that they were moving of their own will. It was only a trick. They were a vast multitude and a great crowd, and each of them threw a staff and a rope, until the valley was full of snakes riding over one another.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿So Moses felt fear within himself﴾, meaning he feared for the people that they would be tempted by their magic and deceived by them before he threw what was in his right hand. So Allah, may He be exalted, revealed to him at that moment: ﴿Throw what is in your right hand﴾, meaning his staff. Then, behold, ﴿it will swallow what they have made.﴾ That is because it became a great, terrifying serpent, with eyes, legs, a neck, a head and fangs. It kept pursuing those ropes and staffs until it left none of them without seizing and swallowing it, while the magicians and the people watched it openly, plainly, in broad daylight in the forenoon. Thus the miracle appeared, the proof became manifest, and what they had been doing was nullified. For this reason He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿What they have made is only a magician's trick, and a magician does not succeed wherever he comes.﴾

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Musa al-Shaybani narrated to us, Hammad ibn Khalid narrated to us, Ibn Mu'adh—I think he is al-Sa'igh—narrated to us, from al-Hasan, from Jundab ibn Abdullah al-Bajali, who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings be upon him) said: "When you seize them—meaning the sorcerer—kill him." Then he recited: ﴿and a magician does not succeed wherever he comes.﴾ He said: "He will not be granted belief wherever he is found."

Al-Tirmidhi has narrated its origin both as a mawquf (a report ending at a Companion, not traced to the Prophet) and as a marfu' (a report traced to the Prophet). [Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 1460, by way of Isma'il ibn Muslim from al-Hasan from Jundab (may Allah be pleased with him). He said: "We do not know this hadith as marfu' except through this route. Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Makki is weak in hadith, while Isma'il ibn Muslim al-Abdi al-Basri, Waki' said, is trustworthy, and he also narrates from al-Hasan. The sound report from Jundab is mawquf. The practice of some people of knowledge among the Companions of the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) and others is in accordance with this." Note: the Hafiz al-Mizzi mentioned this hadith in his book Tuhfat al-Ashraf (2/446) under the musnad of Jundab al-Khayr al-Azdi, not the musnad of Jundab ibn Abdullah al-Bajali (may Allah be pleased with both of them), so let this be noted.]

When the magicians saw that and witnessed it, and they had expertise in the arts of magic, its methods and its forms, they knew with certainty that what Moses had done was not of the kind of magic and tricks, that it was truth without doubt, and that none can do this except the One who says to a thing, "Be," and it is. At that point they fell down prostrate to Allah and said: ﴿We believe in the Lord of the worlds, the Lord of Moses and Aaron.﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 47-48].

For this reason Ibn Abbas and Ubayd ibn Umayr said: "They were magicians at the beginning of the day, and righteous martyrs at the end of the day."

Muhammad ibn Ka'b said: They were eighty thousand.

Al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza said: They were seventy thousand.

Al-Suddi said: Some thirty-odd thousand.

Al-Thawri said, from Abd al-Aziz ibn Rufay', from Abu Thumama: The magicians of Pharaoh were nineteen thousand.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: They were fifteen thousand.

Ka'b al-Ahbar said: They were twelve thousand.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Hamza narrated to us, Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Waqid narrated to us, from his father, from Yazid al-Nahwi, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, who said: The magicians were seventy men; they became magicians in the morning and martyrs by evening.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Musayyab ibn Wadih narrated to us in Makkah, Ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, who said: al-Awza'i said: When the magicians fell down prostrate, Paradise was raised up for them until they looked at it.

He said: It was also mentioned from Sa'id ibn Salam: Isma'il ibn Abdullah ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, regarding His saying: ﴿So the magicians were thrown down prostrate﴾, that he said: "They saw their dwellings being built for them while they were in prostration." Ikrimah and al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazza said likewise.

Ibn Kathir said, may Allah have mercy on him:

Allah, the Exalted, says, reporting the disbelief of Pharaoh, his obstinacy, his tyranny, and his stubborn rejection of the truth with falsehood, when he saw what he saw of the dazzling miracle and the great sign, and saw that those whom he had sought help from had believed in the presence of all the people and had been utterly overcome. He resorted to stubbornness and slander, and turned to using his status and authority against the magicians. So he threatened and warned them, and said: ﴿Have you believed in him before I give you permission?﴾, that is, "Have you affirmed him before I have ordered you to do so, and have you plotted against me in this matter?" He said a statement which he, the magicians, and all of creation knew to be a slander and a lie: ﴿Indeed, he is your chief who taught you magic.﴾ That is, "You only learned magic from Moses, and you agreed, you and he, against me and my subjects, so that you might make it manifest," just as He said in another verse: ﴿Indeed, this is a plot you have plotted in the city to expel its people from it, but you will soon know.﴾ [Al-A'raf 123].

Then he began to threaten them, saying: ﴿So I will surely cut off your hands and your feet on opposite sides, and I will surely crucify you on the trunks of palm trees.﴾ That is, "I will surely make you an example (muthlah), and I will kill you, and I will disgrace you."

Ibn 'Abbas said: "He was the first one to do that." Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And you will surely know whose punishment is more severe and more lasting.﴾ That is, "You say that I and my people are upon misguidance, and you and Moses and his people are upon guidance. You will soon know who will have the punishment and remain in it."

When he attacked them with that and threatened them, their own souls became cheap to them for the sake of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. They said: ﴿We will never prefer you over what has come to us of the clear proofs.﴾ That is, "We will never choose you over the guidance and certainty that have been attained for us." ﴿And over He who created us﴾ may be an oath, and it may be coordinated with "the clear proofs."

They mean: "We will not choose you over our Creator and Originator, who brought us into being from nothing, who began our creation from clay. He alone deserves worship and submission, not you."

﴿So decree what you will decree.﴾ That is, "Do whatever you wish, and whatever your hand can reach." ﴿You can only decree concerning this worldly life.﴾ That is, "Your authority is only in this abode, which is the abode of passing away, while we have turned toward the abode of permanence." ﴿Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins﴾ That is, "the sins that we committed, especially what you compelled us to do of magic in order to oppose the sign of Allah the Exalted and the miracle of His Prophet."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Nu'aym ibn Hammad narrated to us, Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Abu Sa'id, from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿and what you compelled us to do of magic﴾, he said: "Pharaoh took forty boys from the Children of Israel and ordered that they be taught magic in Farama, and said: 'Teach them a teaching that no one on earth will know.'" Ibn 'Abbas said: "They were among those who believed in Moses, and they are among those who said: ﴿Indeed, we have believed in our Lord that He may forgive us our sins and what you compelled us to do of magic.﴾"

'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said likewise.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Khalid ibn Yazid ibn Abi Malik informed us, from his father, who said: It used to be said: Paradise has one hundred degrees; in each degree are one hundred degrees; [In ف and أ: "between"] between each two degrees is as the distance between the heaven and the earth. In them are rubies and ornaments; in each degree is a commander, whom they regard as having superiority and nobility.

In the two Sahihs: "The people of 'Illiyyin see those above them as you see the star that is far away on the horizon of the sky, because of the difference between them." They said: "O Messenger of God, are those the dwellings of the Prophets?" He said: "Yes, by Him in whose hand is my soul, men who believed in God and affirmed the messengers."

[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6555) and Sahih no. (2830), from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd (رضي الله عنه).]

In the Sunan: "Indeed Abu Bakr and Umar are among them, and how excellent they are."

[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3987) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (96).]

* *

His saying: ﴿Gardens of Eden beneath which rivers flow﴾, meaning a permanent abode, and it is a substitute for "the highest ranks." ﴿They will abide therein forever﴾, meaning they will remain eternally. ﴿And that is the reward of one who purifies himself﴾, meaning who cleanses his soul from defilement, filth and polytheism, worships God alone without partner, and affirms the messengers in what they brought of news and command.

The Most High says, informing that He commanded Musa, peace be upon him, when Fir'awn refused to let the Children of Israel go with him, that he should travel with them by night and take them away from the grip of Fir'awn. Allah has explained this situation at length in other than this noble surah. When Musa departed with the Children of Israel, they awoke to find that there was neither a caller nor a responder among them in Egypt. Fir'awn became extremely angry and sent summoners into the cities (*ḥāshirīn*, meaning those who gather the army for him from his lands and *rasātīq*, the rural districts). He said: ﴿Indeed, these are a small band, and indeed they have enraged us﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 54, 55]. Then, when he had gathered his troops and his army was ready, he set out in pursuit of them: ﴿So they pursued them at sunrise﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 60], meaning at the rising of the sun. ﴿Then when the two groups saw each other﴾, meaning each of the two parties looked at the other, ﴿the companions of Musa said, "Indeed, we are overtaken." He said, "No! Indeed, with me is my Lord; He will guide me."﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 61, 62]. Musa stood with the Children of Israel, with the sea in front of them and Fir'awn behind them. At that point Allah inspired him to ﴿strike for them a dry path through the sea﴾. So he struck the sea with his staff and said, "Split open by the permission of Allah." ﴿Then it parted, and each portion was like a great mountain﴾ [Ash-Shu'ara: 63], meaning a great mountain. Allah sent the wind upon the bed of the sea, and it dried it until it became dry like the surface of the earth. Therefore He said: ﴿Strike for them a dry path through the sea, not fearing being overtaken, nor being afraid﴾, meaning, from Fir'awn, ﴿nor fearing [drowning]﴾, meaning, from the sea, that it would drown your people.

Then the Most High said: ﴿So Fir'awn followed them with his soldiers, and there covered them from the sea that which covered them﴾, meaning the sea, ﴿that which covered them﴾, meaning that which is well known and famous. This phrasing is used for a matter that is well known and famous, as the Most High said: ﴿And the overturned cities He hurled down, and covered them with what covered﴾ [An-Najm: 53, 54], and as the poet said:

I am Abu al-Najm, and my poetry is my poetry

meaning: which is known, and it is famous.

And just as Fir'awn preceded them and led them into the sea, misguiding them and not guiding them to the path of right direction, so too ﴿he will precede his people on the Day of Resurrection and lead them into the Fire, and wretched is the watering place to which they are led﴾ [Hud: 98].

Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim, on Surah 20, verses 80–82:

He, may He be exalted, mentions His great favours upon the Children of Israel and His mighty bounties, in that He delivered them from their enemy Pharaoh, and gladdened their eyes by him, while they were looking on at him and his army as they drowned in a single morning, not one of them escaping. As He, may He be exalted, said: [[Addition from MS F.]] ﴿And We drowned the people of Pharaoh while you were looking on﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 50].

Al-Bukhari said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, Abu Bishr narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to Madinah, the Jews were fasting on 'Ashura'. He asked them, and they said: "This is the day on which Allah granted Musa victory over Pharaoh." He said: "We have a greater claim to Musa than you, so fast it." Muslim also related it in his Sahih. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4737); Sahih Muslim, no. (1130).]]

Then, after the destruction of Pharaoh, Allah appointed a time for Musa and the Children of Israel at the side of the right-hand slope of Mount Tur, which is where He spoke to him, where he asked to see Him, and where He gave him the Torah. [[In MS F and A: "hunaka" (there).]] Meanwhile, the Children of Israel worshipped the calf, as He, may He be exalted, will relate shortly.

As for al-Manna wa al-Salwa, the discussion of them has already been given in Surah al-Baqarah [[At the commentary on verse 57 and what follows.]] and elsewhere. Al-Manna is a sweet food that used to descend upon them from the sky. As-Salwa is a bird that would fall upon them, and they would take from each one only what they needed for the day, as a kindness and mercy from Allah towards them and a favour to them. Therefore He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Eat of the good things with which We have provided you, and do not transgress therein, lest My anger descend upon you﴾. That is: eat from this provision which I have given you, and do not transgress regarding My provision by taking it beyond what you need, opposing what I have commanded you. ﴿Lest My anger descend upon you﴾, that is, lest I become angry with you. ﴿And whoever has My anger descend upon him has indeed fallen﴾. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: that is, he has indeed become wretched.

Shufayy ibn Matih said: Indeed, in Hell there is a palace from whose top the disbeliever will be thrown, and he will fall into Hell for forty autumns before he reaches the bottom. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And whoever has My anger descend upon him has indeed fallen﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim related it.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And indeed I am Most Forgiving to he who repents, believes, and does righteous deeds﴾, that is: whoever turns back to Me, I will turn to him in forgiveness for whatever sin he committed, to the extent that He, may He be exalted, forgave those among the Children of Israel who worshipped the calf.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Repents﴾, that is: he turns back from whatever disbelief, polytheism, hypocrisy, or disobedience he was in.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And believes﴾, that is: with his heart. ﴿And does righteous deeds﴾, that is: with his limbs.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then is guided﴾, 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas: that is, then he does not doubt.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿Then is guided﴾, that is: he remains steadfast upon the Sunnah and the Jama'ah (the way of the Prophet and the united community of the Muslims). Similar was narrated from Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and many others of the salaf (the early righteous generations).

Qatadah said: ﴿Then is guided﴾, that is: he adheres to Islam until he dies.

Sufyan al-Thawri said: ﴿Then is guided﴾, that is: he knows that this has a reward.

Here, "thumma" (then) indicates the sequence of one report after another, like His saying: ﴿Then he was among those who believed and advised one another to patience and advised one another to compassion﴾ [Al-Balad: 17].

When Musa (peace be upon him) set out with the Children of Israel after the destruction of Fir'awn (Pharaoh), they arrived "at a people devoted to idols of their own. They said: O Musa, make for us a god just as they have gods. He said: Indeed, you are a people who act in ignorance. Indeed, these people, what they are engaged in will be destroyed, and what they have been doing is in vain" [al-A'raf: 138-139]. Their Lord had appointed for him thirty nights, then completed them with ten more, so the appointed time of his Lord was completed as forty nights, meaning he fasted them by night and by day. This has already been explained in the Hadith of al-Futun (the Hadith of the Trials). Musa (peace be upon him) hastened ahead to Mount Tur and appointed his brother Harun over the Children of Israel. For this reason, the Exalted said: "And what made you hasten from your people, O Musa? He said: They are close behind me," meaning they are coming and will soon arrive near the mountain. "And I hastened to You, my Lord, that You may be pleased." meaning that You may increase Your pleasure with me. "He said: Indeed, We have tested your people after you, and the Samiri has led them astray." Allah the Exalted informed His Prophet Musa of what had occurred after him among the Children of Israel, and of their worship of the calf that the Samiri had made for them. In the Israelite books, it is mentioned that his name was also Harun, and that during this period Allah the Exalted wrote for him the tablets containing the Tawrah (Torah), as the Exalted said: "And We wrote for him on the tablets an admonition concerning all things and a detailed explanation of all things. So take them with strength and enjoin your people to take the best of them. I will show you the abode of the defiantly disobedient" [al-A'raf: 145], meaning the final fate of those who turn away from My obedience and oppose My command.

* *

His saying: "So Musa returned to his people angry and grieved" means that after Allah the Exalted had informed him of this, he returned to them in extreme anger and indignation against them, while he was occupied with their affairs and with receiving the Tawrah, which contained their law and was a source of honour for them. They had worshipped other than Allah, something every intelligent person with sound judgment knows to be false, and their minds and understanding were feeble. For this reason he returned to them angry and grieved. Al-asaf means intense anger.

Mujahid said: "angry and grieved" means "distressed." Qatadah and al-Suddi said: "grieved" means "sorrowful over what his people had done after him."

"He said: O my people, did your Lord not promise you a good promise?" meaning: Did He not promise you, through my tongue, every good in this world and the Hereafter, and a good outcome, as you have witnessed of His help to you against your enemy, your victory over them, and other of His favours upon you? "Has the time seemed long to you?" meaning: in waiting for what Allah had promised you, and in forgetting the blessings He had bestowed before. "Or did you wish that wrath from your Lord should descend upon you?" Here "am" means "bal" (rather), indicating a turn away from the first statement to the second, as if he were saying: Rather, by this action of yours you intended that wrath from your Lord should descend upon you. "So you broke your promise to me." They said, meaning the Children of Israel, in reply to Musa's rebuke and reproach: "We did not break our promise to you by our own power," meaning not by our own ability or choice.

Then they began to offer a feeble excuse, telling him that they had been cautious about the ornaments of the Copts that they had in their possession, which they had borrowed from them when they left Egypt. "So we threw them away," meaning we cast them from us. It has already been mentioned in the Hadith of al-Futun that Harun (peace be upon him) was the one who had commanded them to throw the ornaments into a pit containing fire.

In a narration of al-Suddi, from Abu Malik, from Ibn 'Abbas: Harun only intended that all the ornaments should be gathered in that pit and melted into one mass, so that when Musa returned he would see in it whatever he wished. Then the Samiri came after that and cast upon it that handful which he had taken from the trace of the Messenger. He asked Harun to pray to Allah that his supplication be answered, and Harun prayed for him, not knowing what he intended. So it was answered for him. At that, the Samiri said: "I ask Allah that it become a calf." So it became a calf that had a lowing sound, meaning a voice, as a means of gradual deception, respite, trial and testing. For this reason they said: "So the Samiri cast it, and brought forth for them a calf, a body with a lowing sound."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn 'Ubadah ibn al-Bakhtari narrated to us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Hammad informed us, from Simak, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: that Harun passed by the Samiri while he was carving the calf. He said to him: "What are you doing?" He replied: "I am making what harms and does not benefit." Harun said: "O Allah, give him what he asked for according to what is in his heart." Harun then went on. The Samiri said: "O Allah, I ask You that it should low," and it lowed. Whenever it lowed, they prostrated to it, and whenever it lowed, they raised their heads.

Then he narrated it through another chain from Hammad, and said: "making what benefits and does not harm."

Al-Suddi said: "It used to low and walk."

"They said," meaning those who went astray among them, who were tested by the calf and worshipped it: "This is your god and the god of Musa, but he forgot." meaning Musa had forgotten Him here and gone off to seek Him. This was already mentioned in the Hadith of al-Futun from Ibn 'Abbas, and Mujahid also said this.

Simak narrated from Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: "but he forgot," meaning he forgot to remind you that this is your god.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated, from Hakim ibn Jubayr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: "They said: This is your god and the god of Musa." Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 20, verse 92–94:

He says, reporting about Musa (peace be upon him), when he returned to his people and saw the great matter that had occurred among them, he was filled with rage (ghayz) at that, [[In F: "anger" (ghadaban).]] and threw down the tablets of the Divine that he had in his hand, and seized his brother by the head, dragging him toward himself. We have already presented the full account of this in "al-A'raf" (Surah 7), and we mentioned there the hadith "The report is not like seeing with one's own eyes" (laysa al-khabar ka-l-mu'aynah).

He began to rebuke his brother Harun (Aaron), saying: ﴿What prevented you, when you saw them going astray, from following me?﴾ That is: so that you would inform me of this matter as soon as it occurred. ﴿Have you then disobeyed my command?﴾ That is: concerning what I had previously instructed you, which is His saying: ﴿Take my place among my people, do right, and do not follow the way of the corrupters﴾ [al-A'raf: 142]. He said: ﴿O son of my mother﴾. He addressed him tenderly by mentioning the mother, although he was his full brother through both parents, because mentioning the mother here is more tender and more eloquent, that is, in compassion and affection. For this reason he said: ﴿O son of my mother, do not seize my beard or my head. Indeed, I feared that you would say, "You have caused division among the Children of Israel and did not heed my word."﴾

This is Harun's excuse before Musa for the cause of his delay in not joining him, so that he did not catch up with him to inform him of what had happened of this grave calamity. He said, ﴿Indeed, I feared﴾ that I would follow you and inform you of this, and you would say to me, "Why did you leave them alone and cause division among them?" ﴿and you did not observe my word﴾ That is: you did not heed what I had commanded you when I appointed you as my successor over them.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Harun was in awe of him and obedient to him.

Moses, peace be upon him, says to the Samiri: "What led you to do what you did? And what came over you until you did what you did?"

Muhammad ibn Ishaq related from Hakim ibn Jubayr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: The Samiri was a man from the people of Bajarma, and he was from a people who worshipped cows. The love of worshipping the cow was in his soul, and he had outwardly professed Islam among the Children of Israel. The name of the Samiri was Musa ibn Zufar.

And in another narration from Ibn 'Abbas: [that] [[addition from A.]] he was from Kerman.

Qatadah said: He was from a town called Samarra.

﴿He said: I saw what they did not see﴾, i.e., I saw Gabriel when he came for the destruction of Pharaoh, ﴿so I grasped a handful from the footprint of the Messenger﴾, i.e., from the hoofprint of his horse. This is the well-known view of many of the exegetes, or most of them.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn 'Ammar ibn al-Harith related to us, 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa informed us, Isra'il informed us, from al-Suddi, from Ubayy ibn 'Umara, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: When Gabriel, peace be upon him, descended and ascended with Moses to the heaven, the Samiri saw him among the people, so he grasped a handful from the hoofprint of the horse. He said: Gabriel carried Moses behind him, until, when he approached the gate of the heaven, he ascended, and Allah wrote the tablets [[in F: "And Allah wrote the pens upon the tablets."]] while he was hearing the scratching of the pens on the tablets. When He informed him that his people had been tested after him, he said: Moses descended, took the calf and burned it. Gharib. Mujahid said: ﴿so I grasped a handful from the footprint of the Messenger﴾: he said: from beneath the hoof of Gabriel's horse. He said: And the handful is a fill of the palm, and the handful is with the tips of the fingers.

Mujahid said: The Samiri ﴿threw﴾, i.e., he cast what was in his hand onto the ornaments of the Children of Israel, and it was melted into a calf, a body that had a lowing, the rustling of the wind within it; so it is its lowing.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Yahya related to us, 'Ali ibn al-Madini informed us, Yazid ibn Zuray' related to us, 'Umara related to us, 'Ikrimah related to us: that the Samiri saw the Messenger, and it was cast into his heart that if you take a handful from the footprint of this horse and cast it into something, then I say to it: "Be," and it will be. So he grasped a handful from the footprint of the Messenger, and his fingers stiffened upon the handful. When Moses went to the appointed time, and the Children of Israel had borrowed the ornaments of the people of Pharaoh, the Samiri said to them: "It is only because of this ornament that this has befallen you, so gather it." They gathered it, and they lit a fire upon it, and it melted. The Samiri saw it, and it was cast into his heart that if you were to throw this handful into this, and say "Be," it would be. So he threw the handful and said: "Be," and it became a calf with a lowing. Then he said: ﴿This is your god and the god of Moses﴾.

And for this reason He said: ﴿So I cast it away﴾, i.e., I threw it along with those who threw, ﴿and thus my soul enticed me﴾, i.e., it made it appealing to me, and it pleased me at that time.

﴿He said: Go, for you have in this life that you will say, "No touching"﴾, i.e., just as you took and touched what its taking and touching was not permitted, from the footprint of the Messenger, so your punishment in this world is that you will say: "No touching", i.e., you do not touch people and they do not touch you.

﴿And indeed for you is a appointed time﴾, i.e., the Day of Resurrection, ﴿which you will not fail to meet﴾, i.e., there is no escape for you from it.

Qatadah said: ﴿That you will say, "No touching"﴾: he said: It is a punishment upon them, and their remnants today say: "No touching."

* *

His saying: ﴿And indeed for you is an appointed time which you will not fail to meet﴾: al-Hasan, Qatadah, and Abu Nahik said: You will not be absent from it.

* *

Qatadah said: The calf had turned from gold into flesh and blood; he burned it with fire, then cast it, i.e., its ashes, into the sea. For this reason He said: ﴿Then we will surely scatter it into the sea, scattering.﴾
