Allah, the Exalted, says to His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): Just as We related to you the account of Musa and what happened to him with Fir'awn (Pharaoh) and his hosts, in clear and manifest detail, so likewise do We relate to you the past accounts as they occurred, without addition or deficiency. ﴿And We have certainly given you from Us a reminder﴾, meaning: from Our presence, ﴿a reminder﴾, which is the Great Qur'an, ﴿with which falsehood cannot come from before it or behind it; it is a revelation from One who is All-Wise, Praiseworthy﴾ [Fussilat: 42]. It is the Book that has not been given to any of the Prophets, from the time they were sent until they were concluded with Muhammad (ﷺ), in its completeness, a Book like it does not exist, nor is there one more perfect than it, nor one that more comprehensively contains the account of what came before, the account of what is yet to occur, and the judgment that decides between people. For this reason Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Whoever turns away from it﴾, meaning: denies it and turns away from following it in command and in seeking guidance, and seeks guidance in other than it, then Allah misguides him and leads him to the path of the Blazing Fire. For this reason He said: ﴿Whoever turns away from it will bear on the Day of Resurrection a burden﴾, meaning: a sin, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And whoever among the factions disbelieves in it, the Fire is his promised place﴾ [Hud: 17].

This is general for everyone to whom the Qur'an has reached, from among the Arabs and the non-Arabs, the People of the Book and others, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿That I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches﴾ [al-An'am: 19]. So everyone to whom the Qur'an has reached is a warner to him and a summoner, so whoever follows it is guided, and whoever opposes it and turns away from it goes astray and is wretched in this world, and the Fire is his promised place on the Day of Resurrection. For this reason He said: ﴿Whoever turns away from it will bear on the Day of Resurrection a burden, * abiding therein﴾, meaning: there is no escape for them from it and no release, ﴿and evil will it be for them on the Day of Resurrection as a load﴾, meaning: how evil is the load they carry.

This is general for everyone to whom the Qur'an has reached, from among the Arabs and the non-Arabs, the People of the Book and others, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿That I may warn you thereby and whoever it reaches﴾ [al-An'am: 19]. So everyone to whom the Qur'an has reached is a warner to him and a summoner, so whoever follows it is guided, and whoever opposes it and turns away from it goes astray and is wretched in this world, and the Fire is his promised place on the Day of Resurrection. For this reason He said: ﴿Whoever turns away from it will bear on the Day of Resurrection a burden, * abiding therein﴾, meaning: there is no escape for them from it and no release, ﴿and evil will it be for them on the Day of Resurrection as a load﴾, meaning: how evil is the load they carry.

It is established in a hadith (a report of the Prophet's sayings or actions) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the Trumpet (al-Sur), and he said: "It is a horn that will be blown into." [[Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (2/192) from the hadith of ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr, may Allah be pleased with them both.]]

In the hadith about the Trumpet narrated through Abu Hurayrah, it is said that it is a great horn, whose circumference is as wide as the heavens and the earth, and that Israfil, peace be upon him, will blow into it. The hadith also says: "How can I be at ease when the owner of the horn has put it to his lips, bent his forehead, and is waiting for permission to blow?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what should we say?" He said: "Say: 'Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best Disposer of affairs. In Allah we put our trust.'" [[The hadith was previously mentioned in the discussion of the Trumpet at verse 73 of Surah al-An'am.]]

* *

That is, in the worldly life. Their stay in it was indeed brief, about ten days or so.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿We know best what they say﴾, that is, during their secret conversation among themselves. ﴿When their most intelligent one says: "You stayed no more than a day."﴾ That is, the most perfect in reason among them. ﴿You stayed no more than a day﴾, that is, because the duration of the worldly life seemed short to them on the Day of Return, since all of the world, however many its times recur and its nights and days and hours follow one another, is like a single day. Qatadah said: "with no deviation from him" — they will not turn away from him.

Abu Salih said: "with no deviation from him" — there is no deviation from him.

Ibn Kathir's commentary (Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim) on Surah 20, verses 109–112:

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿On that Day﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection, ﴿intercession will not benefit, except for one whom the Most Merciful has permitted and whose words He approves﴾, meaning in His presence. This is like His saying: ﴿Who is it that can intercede with Him except by His permission?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255]. And His saying: ﴿And how many angels are there in the heavens whose intercession will avail nothing except after Allah gives permission to whom He wills and approves﴾ [al-Najm: 26]. He also said: ﴿And they do not intercede except for those whom He approves﴾ [al-Anbiya': 28]. And He said: ﴿And intercession with Him does not benefit except for the one for whom He has permitted it﴾ [Saba': 23]. And He said: ﴿On the Day when the Spirit and the angels stand in rows, they will not speak except one whom the Most Merciful has permitted, and he will say what is correct﴾ [al-Naba': 38].

In the two Sahihs (al-Sahihayn, the two authentic collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim), narrated through more than one chain, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who is the master of the children of Adam and the most honoured of creation before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that he said: "I will come and fall prostrate beneath the Throne before Allah. He will open to me praises that I cannot count now, and He will leave me as long as Allah wills to leave me. Then He will say: 'O Muhammad, raise your head, speak and you will be heard, intercede and your intercession will be accepted.'" He said: "Then He will set a limit for me, and I will admit them into Paradise. Then I will return," and he mentioned this four times, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him and upon all the prophets.

In the hadith [also] Allah, the Exalted, says: "Bring out of the Fire whoever has in his heart the weight of a grain of faith." So they bring out a great multitude. Then He says: "Bring out of the Fire whoever has in his heart half a mithqal of faith. Bring out of the Fire whoever has in his heart what weighs an atom (dharrah). Bring out whoever has in his heart the least, least, least weight of an atom of faith." This is the hadith in full. [See: the hadiths on intercession under the commentary on verse 79 of Surah al-Isra'.]

* *

His saying: ﴿He knows what is before them and what is behind them﴾, meaning He encompasses all creatures in His knowledge, ﴿but they cannot encompass Him in knowledge﴾. This is like His saying: ﴿And they do not encompass anything of His knowledge except what He wills﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255].

* *

His saying: ﴿And faces will be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and others said: the creatures will submit, be humbled and surrender to their Mighty One, the Ever-Living who does not die. Al-Qayyum is the One who does not sleep, who is the Sustainer of everything, who manages and preserves it. He is perfect in Himself, and everything is in need of Him, and nothing subsists except through Him.

* *

His saying: ﴿And he has failed who carries injustice﴾, meaning on the Day of Resurrection, for Allah will surely render every right to its owner, to the extent that the hornless sheep will be avenged against the horned sheep.

In a hadith: "Allah, the Exalted, says: 'By My might and My majesty, no wrongdoer's injustice will pass Me by today.'"

In the Sahih: "Beware of injustice, for injustice will be darkness on the Day of Resurrection." [Muslim narrated it in his Sahih, no. 2390, from the hadith of Jabir, with the wording: "Beware of injustice, for injustice will be darkness on the Day of Resurrection."] Utter failure belongs to whoever meets Allah while associating partners with Him, for Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, association [with Allah] is a great injustice﴾ [Luqman: 13].

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds while he is a believer will fear neither injustice nor diminution﴾. When He mentioned the wrongdoers and their threat, He followed it with the righteous and their judgment, which is that they will not be wronged nor have anything diminished, meaning their evil deeds will not be increased and their good deeds will not be reduced. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatadah and others. So injustice (zulm) is increase, by having the sin of another placed upon one, and diminution (hadm) is reduction.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 20, verses 113–114:

He says: Since the Day of Return (al-Ma'ad) and the recompense for good and evil is certain to occur without doubt, We sent down the Qur'an as a bringer of glad tidings and a warner, in a clear, eloquent Arabic tongue (lisan 'arabi mubin fasih), with no confusion or incoherence in it. ﴿And We have varied in it some of the warnings, that perhaps they may fear Allah﴾, meaning: that they may abandon sins, prohibited acts and immoralities. ﴿Or it causes them to remember﴾, meaning: it produces obedience and the performance of acts of devotion. ﴿So exalted is Allah, the King, the Truth﴾, meaning: the King, the Truth, is far exalted above imperfection and sanctified, He who is the Truth, whose promise is true, whose threat is true, whose messengers are true, and Paradise is true, and the Fire is true, and everything from Him is true. And it is part of His justice, exalted is He, that He does not punish anyone before warning and the sending of messengers and the establishing of proof against His creation, so that no one will have an argument or a pretext.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you﴾, it is like His saying in the surah "I swear by the Day of Resurrection": ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation. So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation. Then upon Us is its clarification﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 16–19]. And it is established in the Sahih from Ibn 'Abbas that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would struggle with the revelation intensely, and among what he would do was move his tongue, so Allah revealed this verse. The meaning is that when Jibril brought him the revelation, whenever Jibril recited a verse, he would recite it along with him, out of his intense eagerness to memorize the Qur'an. So Allah guided him to what was easier and lighter for him, so that it would not burden him. He said: ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it. Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation﴾, meaning: that We will gather it in your breast, then you will recite it to the people without forgetting any of it. ﴿So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation. Then upon Us is its clarification﴾. And in this verse He said: ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation is completed to you﴾, meaning: rather, listen attentively, and when the angel finishes reciting it to you, then recite it after him. ﴿And say: My Lord, increase me in knowledge﴾, meaning: increase me in knowledge from You.

Ibn 'Uyaynah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The Prophet (ﷺ) continued to increase in [knowledge] until Allah, Mighty and Majestic, took him.

And for this reason it came in a hadith: "Indeed Allah continued to send the revelation upon His Messenger, until the revelation was at its greatest when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died." [Reported by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 4982, from the hadith of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Ibn Majah said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr narrated to us, from Musa ibn 'Ubaydah, from Muhammad ibn Thabit, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "O Allah, benefit me with what You have taught me, teach me what will benefit me, and increase me in knowledge, and all praise is due to Allah in every state." [Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 251, and Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. 3599.]

al-Tirmidhi also narrated it from Abu Kurayb, from 'Abd Allah ibn Numayr, with this chain, and said: "Gharib (strange) from this route." Al-Bazzar narrated it from 'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Fallas, from Abu 'Asim, from Musa ibn 'Ubaydah, with it, and he added at its end: "And I seek refuge in Allah from the condition of the people of the Fire."

And 'Ali ibn Abi Talha narrated the same from him.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And when We said to the angels, "Prostrate to Adam"﴾, He, exalted is He, mentions the honouring and dignifying of Adam, and the preference He gave him over many of His creation.

The discussion of this story has already preceded in Surat al-Baqarah, al-A'raf, al-Hijr and al-Kahf [[See the commentary on the verses: 30-38 of al-Baqarah, 11-24 of al-A'raf, 28-40 of al-Hijr, and 50 of al-Kahf.]] and it will come at the end of Surat Sad [[When commenting on verses 71-85.]] [God willing]. [[Addition from manuscripts F and A.]] In it He mentions the creation of Adam and His command to the angels to prostrate to him, as honour and dignity, and it shows the enmity of Iblis towards the children of Adam and towards their father from of old. Therefore He said: ﴿So they prostrated, except Iblis; he refused﴾, i.e., he refrained and was arrogant. ﴿So We said, "O Adam, indeed this is an enemy to you and to your wife"﴾, meaning Hawwa', peace be upon them both, ﴿so let him not drive you both out of the Garden, lest you be made wretched﴾, i.e., beware lest he strive to get you out of it, and you toil, struggle and become wretched in seeking your provision, for here you are in a pleasant, wholesome life, without hardship or difficulty.

﴿Indeed, it is [granted] to you that you will not go hungry therein, nor be naked﴾. He linked hunger and nakedness together because hunger is the humiliation of the inner self, and nakedness is the humiliation of the outer self.

﴿And that you will not thirst therein, nor be exposed to the sun﴾. These two also are paired: thirst is the heat of the inner self, which is thirst, and ﴿ad-duha﴾ (exposure to the sun) is the heat of the outer self.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Then Satan whispered to him, saying, "O Adam, shall I direct you to the tree of eternity and a kingdom that does not decay?"﴾. It has already been mentioned that he ﴿caused them to fall by deception﴾ [al-A'raf: 22], and ﴿he swore to them, "Indeed, I am to you a sincere advisor"﴾ [al-A'raf: 21]. It has also been mentioned that Allah, exalted is He, revealed to Adam and his wife that they should eat from all the fruits, and not approach this specific tree in the Garden. Iblis kept at them until they ate from it, and it was the tree of eternity, meaning that whoever eats from it will be made eternal and his stay will endure. A hadith has also mentioned the tree of eternity. Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Shu'ba narrated to us from Abu al-Dahhak, I heard Abu Hurayra narrating from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Indeed, in Paradise there is a tree in whose shade a rider travels for a hundred years without crossing it, and it is the tree of eternity." Imam Ahmad also narrated it. [[Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. (2547), and al-Musnad of Imam Ahmad (2/455).]]

As for His saying: ﴿So they both ate from it, and their private parts became apparent to them﴾, Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ishkab narrated to us, 'Ali ibn 'Asim narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatada, from al-Hasan, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah created Adam a tall man with abundant hair on his head, as if he were a tall palm tree. When he tasted the tree, his garment fell from him, and the first thing that appeared of him was his private part. When he looked at his private part he began to run in the Garden, and a tree seized his hair, so he struggled with it. The Merciful called out: 'O Adam, are you fleeing from Me?' When he heard the speech of the Merciful he said: 'O Lord, no, but out of shame.' 'Do you see, if I repent and return, will I return to the Garden?' He said: 'Yes.'" This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Then Adam received from his Lord words, and He accepted his repentance﴾. [[The hadith has been cited under the commentary on verse 37 of al-Baqarah.]]

This is a broken chain (munqati') between al-Hasan and Ubayy ibn Ka'b, as he did not hear it from him, and there is also scrutiny regarding its being traced to the Prophet (ﷺ).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And they began to cover themselves with leaves from the Garden﴾. Mujahid said: "They would patch them together like a garment." Qatada and al-Suddi said the same.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ja'far narrated to us, from Ibn 'Awn, Sufyan narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Layla, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas regarding: ﴿And they began to cover themselves with leaves from the Garden﴾ he said: "They would take off the leaves of the fig tree and place them over their private parts."

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, and so he went astray. Then his Lord chose him, accepted his repentance, and guided him﴾. al-Bukhari said: Qutayba narrated to us, Ayyub ibn al-Najjar narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salama, from Abu Hurayra, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Musa argued with Adam and said to him: 'You are the one who expelled people from the Garden by your sin and made them wretched?' Adam said: 'O Musa, you are the one whom Allah chose with His messages and His speech. Do you blame me for a matter that Allah had written against me before He created me?' or 'had decreed for me before He created me.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "So Adam overcame Musa in argument." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4738).]] This hadith has chains in the Two Sahihs and other collections. [[See Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (4736) and Sahih Muslim, no. (2652).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Anas ibn 'Iyad informed me, from al-Harith ibn Abi Dhubab, from Yazid ibn Hurmuz who said: I heard Abu Hurayra say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Adam and Musa argued before their Lord, and Adam overcame Musa. Musa said: 'You are the one whom Allah created with His own hand, breathed into you of His spirit, made His angels prostrate to you, and settled you in His Garden; then you brought people down to the earth because of your sin?' Adam said: 'You are Musa, whom Allah chose with His message and His speech, and gave you the Tablets in which is the explanation of everything, and brought you near as one who converses privately. How many years before I was created did you find that Allah had written the Torah?' Musa said: 'Forty years.' Adam said: 'Did you find in it: ﴿And Adam disobeyed his Lord, and so he went astray﴾?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'Do you blame me for an act that Allah had written I would do forty years before He created me?'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "So Adam overcame Musa."

al-Harith said: Abd al-Rahman ibn Hurmuz also narrated this to me from Abu Hurayra, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). [[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2652), by way of Anas ibn 'Iyad from al-Harith ibn Abi Dhiab, from Yazid ibn Hurmuz and Abd al-Rahman al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him).]]

His saying: ﴿Then if guidance comes to you from Me﴾ Abu al-'Aliyah said: the prophets, the messengers and the clear explanation.

﴿Whoever follows My guidance will not go astray, nor will he be distressed.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: he will not go astray in this world, and he will not be wretched in the Hereafter.

﴿But whoever turns away from My remembrance﴾ means: whoever opposes My command and what I have sent down to My messenger, turns away from it, forgets it, and takes guidance from other than it. ﴿Indeed, for him is a constricted life﴾ means: in this world. He has no tranquility and no expansion of his breast; rather his chest is [constricted] [[Addition from MS F, A.]] and distressed because of his misguidance. Even if his outward appearance is luxurious, and he wears what he wishes, eats what he wishes, and dwells where he wishes, yet his heart, as long as it has not reached certainty and guidance, is in anxiety, confusion and doubt, and he continually remains in suspicion, vacillating. This is the constriction of life.

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn 'Abbas regarding ﴿indeed, for him is a constricted life﴾: he said, "Misery."

Al-'Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿indeed, for him is a constricted life﴾: he said, "Every wealth I give to a servant of My servants, whether little or much, if he does not fear Me in it, there is no good in it, and that is the constriction in livelihood." It is also said that a group of misguided people turned away from the truth, and they were in worldly abundance and arrogant, so their livelihood became constricted. That is because they thought that Allah would not provide them with their livelihoods, out of their evil opinion of Allah and their denial. When a servant denies Allah, has an evil opinion of Him, and does not trust Him, his livelihood becomes harsh upon him, and that is the constriction.

Al-Dahhak said: it is the evil deed and the corrupt provision. Likewise said 'Ikrimah and Malik ibn Dinar.

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah reported from Abu Hazim, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Sa'id regarding His saying ﴿a constricted life﴾: "His grave will be constricted for him until his ribs interlock within it." Allah says: ﴿Has it not become clear to them﴾ to these deniers of what you have brought them, O Muhammad, how many generations We destroyed before them, those who denied the messengers. They perished, and no remnant, trace, or vestige of them remains, as they witness from their ruined dwellings, which they left behind, walking among them. ﴿Indeed in that are signs for those of understanding﴾, that is, those with sound intellects and upright minds, as Allah says: ﴿Have they not traveled through the land, so that they would have hearts with which to understand or ears with which to hear? For indeed, it is not eyes that are blinded, but blinded are the hearts within the breasts﴾ [Al-Hajj: 46]. And He said in Surah As-Sajdah: ﴿Has it not become clear to them how many generations We destroyed before them, through whose dwellings they walk? Indeed in that are signs. Then will they not hear?﴾ [As-Sajdah: 26].

Allah says: ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord, it would have been inevitable, and a specified term﴾, that is, were it not for the prior decree from Allah, that He does not punish anyone except after the establishment of proof against them, and the specified term that Allah has set for these deniers until an appointed time, the punishment would have come upon them suddenly. Therefore He said to His Prophet, consoling him: ﴿So be patient over what they say﴾, that is, over their denial of you, ﴿and exalt your Lord with praise before the rising of the sun﴾, meaning the Fajr prayer, ﴿and before its setting﴾, meaning the Asr prayer, as has come in the two Sahihs from Jarir ibn Abdullah al-Bajali (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "We were sitting with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon and said: 'Indeed you will see your Lord as you see this moon, and you will not be harmed in seeing Him. (3330), who said: "This is a gharib hadith."]

Ibn Kathir said, quoting Allah, the Exalted, addressing His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ): "Do not look at what We have given to these people of luxury (al-mutrafin) and their like and peers, and at the blessings they have. Indeed, that is only a fleeting flower (zahrah za'ilah) and a passing blessing (ni'mah ha'ilah), by which We test them. And few of My servants are grateful."

Mujahid said: ﴿Pairs of them﴾ means: the wealthy. ﴿Indeed, We have given you [Allah] (ataka [Allah]) better than what We gave them﴾ (the words "Allah" are added in some copies). As He said in another verse: ﴿And We have certainly given you seven of the oft-repeated (verses) and the great Qur'an. Do not extend your eyes toward what We have given to pairs of them﴾ [al-Hijr: 87-88]. Likewise, what Allah, the Exalted, has stored up for His Messenger in the Hereafter is a great matter that cannot be measured or described, as He said: ﴿And your Lord is going to give you, and you will be satisfied﴾ [al-Duha: 5], and for this reason He said: ﴿But the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting﴾.

In the Sahih it is narrated that when 'Umar ibn al-Khattab entered upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in that upper room (mashrabah) in which he had secluded himself from his wives when he had sworn off them, he found him reclining on a mat of palm fibre, and there was nothing in the room except a small heap of qarz (tanning leaves) and a hanging water skin. 'Umar's eyes began to weep, and the Messenger of Allah said: "What makes you weep?"

He said: "O Messenger of Allah, Chosroes and Caesar are in what they are in, while you are the chosen one of Allah from among His creation?" He said: "Are you in doubt, O son of al-Khattab? Those are a people whose good things were hastened to them in their worldly life."

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the most detached from the world while having the ability to possess it. Whenever it came to him, he would spend it in this way and that, on the servants of Allah, and he did not save anything for himself for the morrow.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yunus informed us, Ibn Wahb informed me, Malik informed me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The thing I fear most for you is what Allah opens up for you of the flower (zahrah) of the worldly life." They said: "And what is the flower of the world, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "The blessings of the earth."

Qatadah and al-Suddi said: "Zahrat al-hayat al-dunya" means the adornment of the worldly life. Qatadah said: ﴿That We may test them therein﴾ means: that We may try them.

And His saying: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family and be steadfast in it﴾ means: rescue them from the punishment of Allah by establishing prayer, and be steadfast yourself in performing it, as He said: ﴿O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire﴾ [at-Tahrim: 6].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ahmad ibn Salih told us, Ibn Wahb told us, Hisham ibn Sa'd informed me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from his father: that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab used to spend the night with him, I and Yarfa'. He had a portion of the night in which he would pray, and sometimes he did not sleep, so we would say: "He will not rise tonight as he used to rise." And whenever he woke up (he would establish prayer for his family) – meaning his household – and he would say: ﴿And enjoin prayer upon your family and be steadfast in it﴾.

And His saying: ﴿We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you﴾ means: if you establish prayer, provision will come to you from where you do not expect, as He said: ﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out and will provide for him from where he does not expect﴾ [at-Talaq: 2-3], and He said: ﴿And I did not create jinn and mankind except to worship Me. I do not want from them any provision, and I do not want that they should feed Me. Indeed, Allah is the Provider, the Possessor of strong force, the Firm﴾ [adh-Dhariyat: 56-58]. For this reason He said: ﴿We do not ask you for provision; We provide for you.﴾ Al-Thawri said: ﴿We do not ask you for provision﴾ means: We do not burden you with seeking it.

Ibn Abi Hatim [also] said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj told us, Hafs ibn Ghiyath told us, from Hisham, from his father: that whenever he entered upon the people of the world and saw some of their worldly goods, when he returned to his family and entered the house, he would recite: ﴿And do not extend your eyes﴾ up to His saying: ﴿We provide for you,﴾ then he would say: "The prayer, the prayer; may Allah have mercy on you."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad al-Qatawani told us, Sayyar told us, Ja'far told us, from Thabit, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ), whenever he was afflicted with need (khasasah), would call out to his family: "O my household, pray, pray." Thabit said: And the prophets, whenever a matter befell them, would resort to prayer.

al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah narrated, from the hadith of 'Imran ibn Za'idah, from his father, from Abu Khalid al-Walibi, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah, the Exalted, says: O son of Adam, devote yourself to My worship; I will fill your heart with richness and close off your poverty. And if you do not do so, I will fill your heart with preoccupation and I will not close off your poverty."

Ibn Majah narrated from the hadith of al-Dahhak, from al-Aswad, from Ibn Mas'ud: "I heard your Prophet (ﷺ) say: Whoever makes his concerns one concern, the concern of the Hereafter, Allah will suffice him for the concern of his worldly life. And whoever has his concerns scattered over the affairs of the world, Allah does not care in which valley of it he perishes."

It is also narrated from the hadith of Shu'bah, from 'Umar ibn Sulayman [in some copies: 'Amr ibn Sulaym], from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Aban, from his father, from Zayd ibn Thabit, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever has the world as his concern, Allah scatters his affairs and places his poverty before his eyes, and he will not get from the world except what has been written for him. And whoever has the Hereafter as his intention, Allah gathers his affairs for him, places his richness in his heart, and the world comes to him subdued."

﴿And the good outcome is for piety﴾ means: a good outcome in this world and the Hereafter, which is Paradise, for those who fear Allah.

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said, reporting about the disbelievers and their statement: ﴿Why does he not bring us a sign from his Lord?﴾ That is, "Why does Muhammad not bring us a sign from his Lord," meaning a clear indication of the truth of his claim that he is the Messenger of Allah? Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Has there not come to them clear evidence of what is in the former scriptures?﴾ That is, the Great Qur'an which Allah revealed to him, while he was unlettered (ummi), unable to write, and had not studied with the People of the Book. In it there came reports of the earlier peoples, of what happened to them in bygone ages, in agreement with the sound earlier books where they are correct, for the Qur'an is a guardian over them (muhaymin): it confirms what is sound in them and clarifies the error of what has been falsified in them and attributed to them. This verse is like His saying in Surah al-'Ankabut: ﴿And they say, "Why are no signs sent down upon him from his Lord?" Say, "The signs are only with Allah, and I am only a clear warner." Is it not sufficient for them that We have sent down to you the Book being recited to them? Indeed in that is mercy and a reminder for a people who believe.﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 50-51]

In the Sahih it is narrated from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "There is no prophet except that he was given signs such that people believed in the like of them, but what I was given is a revelation which Allah revealed to me, and I hope that I will have the most followers on the Day of Resurrection." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4981, from Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him).]

Here He mentioned the greatest of the signs given to him, peace be upon him, which is the Qur'an. He has miracles that cannot be limited or counted, as is recorded in his books and established in their places.

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And if We had destroyed them with a punishment before it, they would have said, "Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger so we could follow Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced?"﴾ That is, if We had destroyed these deniers before We sent to them this noble Messenger and sent down to them this great Book, they would have said: ﴿Our Lord, why did You not send to us a messenger?﴾ before You destroyed us, so that we might believe in him and follow him. As He said: ﴿so that we would follow Your signs before we were humiliated and disgraced.﴾ Allah the Exalted explains that these deniers are obstinate, stubborn and hostile, and will not believe: ﴿And even if every sign came to them, until they see the painful punishment.﴾ [Yunus: 97] As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And this is a blessed Book which We have sent down, so follow it and fear Allah that you may receive mercy, lest you say, "The Book was only sent down to two groups before us, and indeed we were unaware of their study," or say, "If the Book had been sent down to us, we would have been better guided than they." There has certainly come to you clear evidence from your Lord, and guidance and mercy. So who is more unjust than one who denies the signs of Allah and turns away from them? We will reward those who turn away from Our signs with a terrible punishment for what they used to turn away.﴾ [al-An'am: 155-157] And He said: ﴿And they swore by Allah their strongest oaths that if a warner came to them, they would be better guided than any of the nations. But when a warner came to them, it increased them only in aversion.﴾ [Fatir: 42] And He said: ﴿And they swore by Allah their strongest oaths that if a sign came to them they would surely believe in it. Say, "Signs are only with Allah." And what will make you realize that when they come they will not believe? And We will turn their hearts and their eyes away, just as they did not believe in it the first time, and We will leave them in their transgression, wandering blindly.﴾ [al-An'am: 109-110]

Then Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say﴾, that is, O Muhammad, to whoever denies you, opposes you and persists in his disbelief and obstinacy: ﴿Each is waiting⁠—﴾ that is, from us and from you ﴿so wait⁠—﴾ that is, await, ﴿and you will come to know who are the people of the even path⁠—﴾ that is, the straight way, ﴿and who is guided⁠—﴾ to the truth and the path of right guidance. This is like His saying: ﴿And they will know, when they see the punishment, who is more astray in path.﴾ [al-Furqan: 42] And: ﴿They will know tomorrow who is the liar, the insolent.﴾ [al-Qamar: 26]

The end of the tafsir of Surah Taha, and to Allah belongs all praise and favor.
